news.originalContent:
As Eisenkot’s bloc moves to form a government and courts the ultra-Orthodox, the Gaza genocide and settler pogroms continue.

Israel’s parliament speaker is due to be replaced on Tuesday, one of several signs that power is being rearranged as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc angles to lead the government.

But for Palestinians, the machinery of occupation, dispossession and deprivation keeps running. Israeli attacks killed at least 37 people in Gaza in the past week, while in the occupied West Bank, settlers attacked whole villages with little to stop them.

The past week saw numerous Israeli attacks and killings in Gaza, as military claims of targeting fighters were weighed against accounts of people killed in tents, filling water containers and driving to a wedding photo shoot. According to Gaza’s Ministry of Health, as of November 16, Israel has killed 1,650 Palestinians since the October 2025 “ceasefire”.

On November 12, an Israeli bomb hit the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis. The hospital’s surgery building was struck, killing six people, including surgeon Rizq Abu Shaira, and wounding dozens. The Israeli military said it targeted Hamas’s Khan Younis Brigade commander, Muhammad Abu Ismail, and accused Hamas of running a command centre in the hospital. In the days that followed, the foreign ministers of 18 Arab and Muslim-majority countries condemned the attack as a violation of international humanitarian law.

Beyond the hospital bombing, the Israeli military told Israeli media it had killed 10 Hamas operatives in the past week. Among them was Samir Abu Younis, whom the army named as Hamas’s Rafah Brigade commander, killed in a drone strike in al-Mawasi on November 14, which Hamas confirmed. The strike hit a tent for displaced people, wounding two. Over the weekend, in Jabalia camp, two men were killed in a strike the army said targeted “terrorists”, and a separate strike on a Gaza government security post in al-Mawasi, Rafah, killed two people, according to Wafa.

At the same time, Israeli forces continued to kill Palestinians in circumstances that offered little indication of any military target:

This week, Gaza’s Health Ministry recorded the winter’s first death from hypothermia – a nine-month-old baby – following the devastation of last week’s rains. Israel’s Prime Minister’s Office claimed more than 91,000 tents and 8,200 trucks of winter supplies have been delivered, the Times of Israel reported, and blamed Hamas for the suffering. The United Nations, however, reported this week that aid-truck offloads have fallen about 42 percent after Israel suspended the Egyptian corridor.

The United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Italy called conditions in Gaza “catastrophic” and urged that 150,000 tents be allowed into the territory.

The most violent olive harvest on record continues in the occupied West Bank, as OCHA counted 410 harvest-related attacks this year as of November 9. The week saw several kinds of attacks by settlers and soldiers unfold repeatedly across the West Bank:

But in the past week, two settler attacks escalated into full-blown pogroms against Palestinian communities. Late on November 10, more than 50 masked settlers set fire to a scrapyard, a workshop and cars beside homes in al-Lubban Asharqiya, south of Nablus, burning more than 100 vehicles and dozens of olive trees and cutting power. Wafa put the damage from the attack at more than one million shekels ($310,000). On November 12, after soldiers evicted an outpost near Atara, north of Ramallah, settlers smashed four homes and a factory and wrecked at least three cars, injuring more than 10 residents.

The Israeli army evacuated outposts near Burqa, Wadi al-Rakhim and Jalud, and on November 11, police arrested four Israelis over a September attack by settlers on troops escorting a displaced Palestinian family, the Times of Israel reported.

Yet settlers re-established an outpost at Burqa within days, and in Wadi al-Rakhim, south of Yatta, the six-week siege of Yousef Shanaran’s home by settlers continues unimpeded. While soldiers pulled down the settlers’ tent outside Shanaran’s home on November 13, the tent was rebuilt after sunset, according to the family. On November 16, Shanaran told Al Jazeera that settlers had thrown stones at their home throughout the previous night. Soldiers were present, but did nothing. “We are alone,” he declared.

As the occupation continues largely unchecked, early coalition negotiations suggest that a change of government might mean little more than a rearrangement of the political chairs for Palestinians. On November 10, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told the new parliament in a speech Eisenkot called “hate-filled” that Arab-led parties “seek to destroy the Jewish state”, while demanding a Zionist unity government instead of the opposition partnering with the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel.

Meanwhile, Israel’s Channel 12 reported on November 15 that Netanyahu’s chief of staff had given police the tip behind three election-day arrests of activists from Ra’am, one of the Arab-led parties. Israel’s attorney general is probing whether Netanyahu’s office engineered the case to bolster claims that Arab parties stole the vote. Shin Bet chief David Zini also asked to wiretap five Palestinian members of the Israeli parliament, Channel 12 reported. Netanyahu’s office has called the report defamatory.

Eisenkot called the campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel “racist and violent” and said Netanyahu was a threat to Israeli democracy who could not stay “for even one more minute”.

Yet he has ruled out a government with the Arab parties, whose 19 seats would give his bloc 67, above the 61-seat majority threshold.

Instead, the week’s moves point towards Eisenkot working with the ultra-Orthodox: right-wing anti-Netanyahu leader Avigdor Liberman, just approved as chair of the parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee, suggested working with military leaders, the High Court and religious leaders to compromise on any ultra-Orthodox conscription bill, the Times of Israel reported.

Yet settlers re-established an outpost at Burqa within days, and in Wadi al-Rakhim, south of Yatta, the six-week siege of Yousef Shanaran’s home by settlers continues unimpeded. While soldiers pulled down the settlers’ tent outside Shanaran’s home on November 13, the tent was rebuilt after sunset, according to the family. On November 16, Shanaran told Al Jazeera that settlers had thrown stones at their home throughout the previous night. Soldiers were present, but did nothing. “We are alone,” he declared.

As the occupation continues largely unchecked, early coalition negotiations suggest that a change of government might mean little more than a rearrangement of the political chairs for Palestinians. On November 10, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told the new parliament in a speech Eisenkot called “hate-filled” that Arab-led parties “seek to destroy the Jewish state”, while demanding a Zionist unity government instead of the opposition partnering with the parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel.

Meanwhile, Israel’s Channel 12 reported on November 15 that Netanyahu’s chief of staff had given police the tip behind three election-day arrests of activists from Ra’am, one of the Arab-led parties. Israel’s attorney general is probing whether Netanyahu’s office engineered the case to bolster claims that Arab parties stole the vote. Shin Bet chief David Zini also asked to wiretap five Palestinian members of the Israeli parliament, Channel 12 reported. Netanyahu’s office has called the report defamatory.

Eisenkot called the campaign against Palestinian citizens of Israel “racist and violent” and said Netanyahu was a threat to Israeli democracy who could not stay “for even one more minute”.

Yet he has ruled out a government with the Arab parties, whose 19 seats would give his bloc 67, above the 61-seat majority threshold.

Instead, the week’s moves point towards Eisenkot working with the ultra-Orthodox: right-wing anti-Netanyahu leader Avigdor Liberman, just approved as chair of the parliament’s Foreign Affairs and Defence Committee, suggested working with military leaders, the High Court and religious leaders to compromise on any ultra-Orthodox conscription bill, the Times of Israel reported.

The body of a slain woman was discovered “lying in the leaves” near a popular trail just hours after she arrived at the scenic spot with her recently adopted dog — which was found unharmed days later.

A shocked bystander stumbled upon the body of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, last Wednesday while walking on the trails between Northlake Nature Center and Pelican Park in St. Tammany Parish, according to the St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office.

Rodriguez was found dead, “lying in the leaves,” roughly an hour and a half after arriving in the wooded area with her dog, Evie, in her silver Honda Civic around 12:30 p.m., according to cops and Nola.com.

Her death has since been ruled a homicide, though authorities have not yet released information about the cause of her death.

Rodriguez’s dog, Evie, whom she recently adopted, was located and picked up by a good Samaritan days after the tragedy, according to the St. Tammany Parish Department of Animal Services.

Evie suffered no physical injuries or wounds, and Rodriguez’s family has since claimed her, the department said.

A heartbreaking GoFundMe fundraiser started by Rodriguez’s sister for her burial and funeral costs described her as the “baby of the house.”

“Lizeht Rodriguez was only 24 years old and had her whole life ahead of her. She was the baby of the house, and losing someone so young is unbearable,” Nayma Rodriguez wrote in the fundraiser statement.

“The pain has affected every part of our daily lives. Right now, our family is struggling to work because of the extreme grief we are carrying.”

Investigators said they can’t yet rule out that a stranger killed Rodriguez on the popular trails, where there are no cameras.

“We cannot rule out the possibility of the murder being [done by] a stranger to Lizeht,” Interim Sheriff Bret Ibert said at a press conference on Friday, Nola.com reported.

Police have urged anyone near Pelican Park or the Northlake Nature Center last Wednesday between noon and 2 p.m. to contact investigators and review photos and dashcam footage — emphasizing that no detail is too small.

“Even if you believe you saw nothing unusual, we encourage you to think back to that afternoon. Did you notice anything that seemed out of place?” the St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office wrote in a Facebook post.

“No detail is too small. Please do not assume someone else has already reported what you saw,” the department wrote.

“We ask the public to continue being vigilant, but not to spread fear or speculation,” the statement said. “Our priority remains finding answers for Lizeht’s family and bringing the person responsible to justice.”

Anyone with information is asked to contact the St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office at 985-898-2338.

LeBron James sat out the 76ers’ 135-123 victory in Brooklyn on Monday, one day after moving even higher on the NBA’s all-time assists list.

The 41-year-old James missed his fourth game of the season — all wins — due to management of a lower-back injury, sitting out the second night of back-to-back games.

The NBA’s all-time scoring leader passed former Nets point guard Jason Kidd for third on the all-time assists list in Sunday’s win over the Pacers.

The Sixers also posted wins over the Hornets, the Bucks and the Raptors in the previous games James missed during his first season in Philadelphia. He is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists in his first 11 appearances.

Joel Embiid netted a season-best 37 points in his return to the Sixers lineup after sitting out their win over Indiana to manage a foot issue.

Nets forward Josh Minott was fined $25,000 by the NBA for making an obscene gesture late in Saturday’s game against the Grizzlies.

The 23-year-old Minott is averaging 3.4 points in 6.7 minutes per game, including just two minutes played in Sunday’s loss. The Nets signed the 6-8 forward to a two-year deal worth $9 million over the summer.

Nets leading scorer Michael Porter Jr. had 25 points in his return to the starting lineup for the Nets after he sat out Sunday’s loss in Memphis for personal reasons. He replaced Noah Clowney, who had played 35 minutes in his first start of the season against the Grizzlies.

Nolan Traore replaced Danny Wolf and tied his career high with 23 points on 7-for-12 shooting in 30 minutes.

Wolf had started the previous four games at shooting guard after receiving five DNP’s earlier in the season. He averaged 11.3 points as a starter since contributing 13 off the bench Nov. 4, in a win over Charlotte.

news.originalContent:
The ongoing Israeli assault continues to have disastrous consequences for the people of southern Lebanon.

Kfar Reman, Lebanon – It was the morning of September 7 when we arrived at the site of an Israeli attack in the village of Kfar Reman in southern Lebanon. Bulldozers were digging through the rubble of a home destroyed in an overnight air strike, searching for the bodies of two children.

Ten members of the same family, spanning three generations, had already been found in the building’s collapsed rooms, among them two survivors.

Two months later, I met 10-year-old Zainab and her eight-year-old brother Mustafa. After losing their parents and elder sister, Fatima, and their one-month-old brother, Ahmed, they now live with their grandmother. Both were thrown out of the house due to the intensity of the blast, but their physical wounds were no longer visible.

Zainab had a constant smile, but she was hiding sadness which she did not know how to express in words.

Mustafa was different. There was no smile. He is angry at Israel. When I asked him to share his story or a message to the world instead of speaking to me, he looked straight at the camera.

“What they did is they took my home and my parents from me,” Mustafa said. He paused for a few seconds and continued, “Because of them I no longer live in peace.”

More than a thousand children were injured in Israeli attacks between March and August this year, according to the United Nations.

Some lost a parent or both their parents while more than 260 were killed. That figure represents an average of seven children killed or injured every day over those six months – nearly double the number at the start of the latest on-again, off-again conflict between Hezbollah and Israel in late 2023.

We have repeatedly filmed children’s clothes, toys and school books among the rubble of homes destroyed in Israeli strikes, and repeatedly attended funerals of children killed alongside their parents. It is just as difficult emotionally to talk to survivors who show signs of trauma and tell us they live in fear.

In the village of Tibnine, close to the northern edge of the area occupied by the Israeli army, 11-year-old Bannine took us to the second floor of an orphanage, to show us what a nearby Israeli air strike did to their rooms.

“We were not here when this happened,” Bannine told us in a room full of debris and broken glass. Stuffed animals and clothes were still scattered on the floor.

Hundreds of thousands of people returned to their villages in southern Lebanon because of a reduction in violence in recent months. But there is little sense of security, with Israeli strikes and home demolitions continuing in front line areas.

“We wake up and sleep to the sound of bombing and warplanes and irritating drones,” Anaya Sultan told us. Her father was killed when the Israeli military escalated the conflict earlier this year. “He was my soul … he was everything to me,” she added.

Some of the girls here are not orphans, but their parents are too poor to care for them. According to Lebanese officials, the region’s economy is in a state of collapse.

Recurring conflicts, ruined infrastructure, blocked access to agricultural land, and mass displacement are making it hard for families in southern Lebanon to sustain themselves.

The UN identified southern Lebanon – alongside impoverished northern and eastern regions such as Akkar and Baalbek – as areas of greatest concern where families are struggling to survive.

According to a joint report released by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), the World Food Programme (WFP), and Lebanon’s Ministry of Agriculture, more than 1 million people in Lebanon – about 21 percent of the recorded population – are facing crisis levels of acute food insecurity.

“Unfortunately, so many people are displaced … many of them used to support and help us. They are not present and they themselves are struggling,” Bassima Fawaz, who helps manage the orphanage, told us as we walked through the cold hallways and rooms of the building.

“We had to cover the windows with plastic sheeting because there’s no money to replace the glass shattered by Israeli bombardment. One of our girls is in hospital with pneumonia.”

The Rangers have another injury concern to navigate after all.

Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Mollie Walker about the inside buzz on the Rangers.

Pavel Dorofeyev missed the game against the Canadiens on Monday with a lower-body injury despite head coach Mike Sullivan saying the past two days that he wasn’t concerned about Dorofeyev — who exited their practice Sunday for precautionary reasons — missing time. Sullivan said Monday morning that Dorofeyev participated in their optional morning skate.

Will Cuylle took Dorofeyev’s spot on the second line and scored a pair of goals, while Matt Rempe drew into the lineup for just the sixth time this season and skated on the fourth line. Eeli Tolvanen moved up to the third line, joining Noah Laba and Oliver Bjorkstrand.

When asked what went into ultimately keeping Dorofeyev out, Sullivan just said he was being evaluated for the injury.

In a season already filled with injuries, Dorofeyev’s added another one to their list. Their campaign was altered in the sixth game, when franchise goaltender Igor Shesterkin sustained a season-ending knee injury. Joe Veleno is on long-term injured reserve.

Alberts Smits and Sean Durzi are on injured reserve too. Joonas Korpisalo didn’t make his season debut until Nov. 7 — and didn’t make his MSG debut with the Blueshirts until Monday.

Dorofeyev, for all the posts he’s hit and the goals he hasn’t scored through his opening 21 games with the Rangers, remained at the center of their campaign. With his one-timer and left-handed shot, Dorofeyev, who scored 72 goals across the last two seasons and managed 20 on the power play last year, was added to help anchor their man-advantage unit and inject scoring into the Rangers lineup.

And for at least one night, they needed to operate without him.

Monday night was the Rangers Centennial Capstone Game, marking 100 years to the day since the franchise’s first game against the Montreal Maroons. They held a pregame ceremony — led by former play-by-play announcer Sam Rosen — that featured former players, or representatives from their families, who had their numbers retired by the organization. Mike Richter, Adam Graves, Brian Leetch, Mark Messier and Henrik Lundqvist were the former players in attendance on the ice.

The daughter of Harry Howell, the wife of Rod Gilbert, the daughter of Eddie Giacomin, the granddaughter of Jean Ratelle and the granddaughter of Vic Hadfield were also present on the ice. Billy Dea, the oldest living Rangers alumnus at 93 years old, sent a video that played on the videoboard during a commercial break in the third period.

Scott Morrow’s goal marked his first since March 2025 and first with the Rangers since the trade that sent K’Andre Miller to the Hurricanes. He said he didn’t see it go in from his vantage point at the blue line, but he said, “It was cool to score at Madison Square Garden. Felt good.” … Miller picked up an assist on Cuylle’s first goal and moved within two of 500 for his career. … Defenseman Sean Durzi participated in the Rangers’ optional morning skate in a regular blue jersey, shedding the red non-contact one, and skated with the extras afterward. He hasn’t played since Oct. 26. … Defenseman Marc Del Gaizo was assigned to AHL Hartford postgame. … Joonas Korpisalo became the first goaltender to win his first three starts with the Rangers since Antti Raanta in 2015-16 and just the seventh in franchise history.

Racing at about 71km (44 miles) per second, they burn up as bright streaks, sometimes leaving glowing trails that hang in the sky for seconds.

In this visual explainer, see how the shower forms as Earth crosses a comet’s dust trail, then search for your city to find the best viewing time.

A meteor shower happens when dozens, or sometimes hundreds, of “shooting stars” streak across the night sky. In reality, they are not stars, but tiny bits of space debris burning up in Earth’s atmosphere.

Most of this debris comes from comets, which are icy bodies that orbit the sun and shed dust as they get closer to it. When Earth’s orbit crosses one of these dust trails, the particles, called meteoroids, hit the atmosphere at high speed and heat up. They glow as meteors and usually burn up long before reaching the ground.

The Leonids come from Comet Tempel-Tuttle, whose dust trail Earth passes through every November. Drag the slider below to follow Earth through 2026 and see when it meets the stream.

The Leonids are named after the constellation Leo, the point in the sky from which they appear to come. They are known for fireballs, which are unusually bright meteors from larger bits of debris. They also produce Earth-grazers, meteors that skim the upper atmosphere at a shallow angle and leave long trails near the horizon.

What really sets them apart is their storms. Comet Tempel-Tuttle passes close to the sun about every 33 years and leaves debris behind. When that happens, the shower can produce a storm of at least 1,000 meteors an hour.

The 1833 storm over North America helped scientists work out where meteors come from. In 1966, thousands of meteors fell every minute for about 15 minutes. The most recent storms came in 1999, 2001 and 2002, and the comet next swings close to the sun in 2031.

The Leonids can appear in any part of the sky, so the best approach is to find a dark spot with a wide view, lie back and take in as much sky as you can.

If you trace their paths backwards, the meteors all seem to streak out from a single point known as the radiant. This is an effect of perspective: the debris travels along roughly parallel paths, but the meteors appear to spread out from one point, much like railway tracks seem to meet in the distance.

For the Leonids, the radiant lies in the constellation Leo, which rises in the east around midnight.

According to the International Meteor Organization (IMO), the Leonids are active from November 6 to 30 and are expected to peak on the night between November 17 and 18, around 23:45 GMT on Tuesday. Under clear, dark skies, the IMO expects up to about 15 meteors an hour at the peak.

The best time to watch is between midnight and dawn, as Leo climbs higher in the sky. The moon, which will be about half full on the peak night, sets around midnight in many places, leaving darker skies for the rest of the night.

Find a spot away from city lights and give your eyes about 20 minutes to adjust to the dark.

Use the widget below to find the best viewing times in your city.

Yes. The Leonids are visible from the Northern Hemisphere and the Southern Hemisphere, but conditions are generally better in the north, where Leo climbs higher in the sky. South of the equator, the best chance is in the hour or two before dawn.

Only slightly. The moon reaches its first quarter on November 17 and sets around midnight, so it should not interfere much during the best viewing hours.

The Leonids are far from the busiest shower. Under ideal conditions, the IMO puts their peak rate at about 15 meteors an hour, compared with about 100 for the Perseids in August and about 150 for the Geminids in December. What they lack in numbers, they make up for in speed and their history of storms.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Leon Neal/Getty Images)

Britain has opened an investigation into Russell Brand for telling supporters from prison that he is innocent.

Downing Street called the message appalling and said it is being urgently investigated, the BBC reported. The government expects action if the comedian broke prison rules. His wife, Laura, read the statement on the couple’s Sunday Service show on YouTube, the BBC stated.

“As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening,” Brand said in the message. (RELATED: Russell Brand’s Wife Breaks Silence By Reading His Jailhouse Message)

Prison rules bar inmates from making statements that distress victims, the prime minister’s spokesman told the BBC. Media contact is allowed only in rare cases. “Prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments,” the spokesman said.

The restriction predates Brand. Guidance from 2010 lets inmates reach the media by letter, phone or visit only in exceptional cases, according to the Ministry of Justice instruction PSI 37/2010. It sits under Prison Rules 34 and 35 across England and Wales.

Labour Justice Secretary Alex Norris called the broadcast “completely unacceptable,” the BBC reported. He said on X that he expects action if Brand broke the rules.

The broadcast of a statement from Russell Brand is completely unacceptable. Prisoners are rightly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims. This is being urgently investigated, and I expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules.

Prison governors can cut social visits or strip privileges such as gym time and television, the BBC stated. They can also block phone numbers or increase call monitoring.

The innocence claims will “certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it,” Andrea Simon, the victims’ commissioner for London, told BBC Radio 4.

A jury convicted Brand of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. A judge sentenced him Nov. 9 to 10 years and six months. A jury acquitted him of two other rape counts and one attempted indecent assault, according to the Daily Wire. Officials moved him from HMP Wandsworth to HMP Littlehey, a prison that mainly holds sex offenders, the BBC reported.

news.originalContent:
در خیابان‌های جده، جایی که رفت‌وآمد خودروها با ضرباهنگ شهری که به‌سرعت در حال دگرگونی است درهم می‌آمیزد، زنی جوان که در عربستان سعودی متولد و بزرگ شده، با موتورسیکلت خود مسیرش را باز می‌کند.

برای صدف محمد شریف، که خود را «سم» معرفی می‌کند، موتورسیکلت تنها یک سرگرمی یا راهی برای پر کردن اوقات فراغت نبوده، بلکه بخشی از سفری شخصی برای بازیابی اعتمادبه‌نفس و احساس استقلال بوده است.

این زن جوان که خود را از کودکی شیفته ماجراجویی توصیف می‌کند، می‌گوید آشنایی‌اش با موتورسیکلت در دوره‌ای دشوار از زندگی‌اش آغاز شد؛ زمانی که به گفته خودش «نیاز داشتم از خانه بیرون بیایم، تعادل پیدا کنم و خودم را دوباره به دست بیاورم.»

داستان سم در زمانی روایت می‌شود که زندگی زنان در عربستان سعودی شاهد دگرگونی‌های اجتماعی و اقتصادی شتابانی است؛ تحولاتی که در چند سال گذشته بیش از پیش آشکار شده‌اند.

اجازه رانندگی به زنان در ژوئن ۲۰۱۸ یکی از نمادین‌ترین تغییرات در این مسیر بود. پیش از آن، زنان در عربستان سعودی برای دهه‌ها اجازه رانندگی نداشتند.

بر اساس آمار سازمان کل آمار عربستان سعودی، بین ژوئن ۲۰۱۸ تا ژانویه ۲۰۲۰، در مجموع ۱۷۴ هزار و ۶۲۴ گواهینامه رانندگی برای زنان صادر شد.

دولت عربستان می‌گوید این تحول در چارچوب «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰» قرار دارد که افزایش مشارکت زنان در بازار کار را یکی از اهداف خود تعیین کرده است.

مشارکت زنان سعودی در بازار کار از هدف اولیه ۳۰ درصدی چشم‌انداز عبور کرده و مقام‌ها را واداشته است هدف را به ۴۰ درصد تا سال ۲۰۳۰ افزایش دهند.

اما ارقام اقتصادی به‌ تنهایی همه داستان تغییر اجتماعی را روایت نمی‌کنند.

در زندگی روزمره، برخی زنان همچنان در حال آزمودن مرزهای تازه آن چیزی هستند که از نظر اجتماعی معمول تلقی می‌شود؛ چه در کار، ورزش، رفت‌وآمد یا دنبال کردن سرگرمی‌هایی که به‌طور سنتی با مردان مرتبط بوده‌اند.

تجربه سم در همین چارچوب قرار می‌گیرد.

سم می‌گوید در آغاز، مانند بسیاری از کسانی که برای نخستین بار موتورسیکلت‌سواری را امتحان می‌کنند، «ترسیده و مضطرب» بود.

او به بی‌بی‌سی عربی می‌گوید حتی نمی‌دانست چگونه تعادلش را حفظ کند.

مربی‌اش به او توصیه کرد ابتدا دوچرخه‌سواری یاد بگیرد و بعد به تمرین موتورسیکلت برگردد.

سم همین کار را کرد. ابتدا یاد گرفت چگونه تعادل بدنش را روی دوچرخه حفظ کند، سپس به موتورسیکلت برگشت، بر ترسش غلبه کرد و تعادل بیشتری پیدا کرد.

به گفته او، همین گام کوچک آغاز یک تحول بزرگ‌تر بود.

در شروع، احساس «تنها بودن» در محیط اطرافش همیشه همراهش بود. دیدن زنی که در خیابان‌های عربستان موتورسیکلت می‌راند هم صحنه‌ای معمول نبود، اما او تصمیم گرفت ادامه دهد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وقتی به پنج سال پیش برمی‌گردد، به یاد می‌آورد که چگونه با تحسین به موتورسواران نگاه می‌کرد؛ افرادی که برای او نماد قدرت و استواری بودند. موتورسیکلت‌های بزرگ، لباس‌های ایمنی و مهارت موتورسواران در کنترل وسیله‌ای سنگین و پرسرعت، او را مجذوب خود کرده بود.

می‌گوید: «می‌خواستم مثل آن‌ها باشم، قوی و مستقل.»

با گذشت زمان، این علاقه به تمرین مداوم و سپس به مهارتی حرفه‌ای تبدیل شد؛ مهارتی که به او امکان داد به مربی رسمی موتورسواری تبدیل شود.

بعدتر، سم همراه چند زن دیگر در جده یک گروه زنان موتورسوار با نام «دختران موتورسوار» راه‌اندازی کرد و از طریق شبکه‌های اجتماعی گروهش را معرفی کرد تا زنان بیشتری را به این ورزش ترغیب کند.

اعضای گروه در صفحه اینستاگرام خود، ویدئوهایی از سفرها و تمرین‌هایشان منتشر می‌کنند و به زنان جوان دیگری که می‌خواهند موتورسیکلت‌سواری یاد بگیرند اما نمی‌دانند از کجا شروع کنند یا از چه کسی راهنمایی بگیرند، مشورت می‌دهند.

تعداد اعضای جامعه زنان موتورسوار که سم بنیان گذاشته به حدود ۱۷۰ نفر رسیده است.

او می‌گوید: «دیگر یک گروه کوچک نیستیم، به شبکه‌ای تبدیل شده‌ایم که در آن از یکدیگر حمایت می‌کنیم.»

به گفته سم، تاکنون بیش از ۲۰۰ زن از طریق این گروه برای توسعه و بهبود مهارت‌های موتورسیکلت‌سواری خود حمایت و کمک دریافت کرده‌اند.

او می‌گوید بسیاری از اعضا بسیار فعال‌اند، به‌ویژه در تمرین منظم. آن‌ها بیشتر آخرهفته‌ها برای موتورسواری و شرکت در فعالیت‌ها و رویدادهای مختلف بیرون می‌روند، از جمله «تور اکتبر صورتی» و «تور روز ملی عربستان»، و همچنین مجموعه‌ای گسترده از برنامه‌های اجتماعی و رویدادهای موتورسیکلت‌سواری که در طول سال برگزار می‌شوند.

سم امیدوار است در آینده یک مدرسه رسمی و از نظر قانونی به‌رسمیت‌شناخته‌شده برای آموزش موتورسیکلت‌سواری تاسیس کند تا بتواند آموزش تخصصی را در چارچوب‌ها و استانداردهای مورد تائید ارائه دهد.

سم خود را تنها زن موتوسوار نمی‌داند، بلکه خود را بخشی از نسلی از زنان در عربستان می‌بیند که فضاهای تازه‌ای را در زندگی عمومی تجربه می‌کنند.

داده‌های رسمی تازه نشان می‌دهند حضور زنان سعودی در حوزه‌هایی خارج از نقش‌های سنتی در حال گسترش است.

بر اساس آمار رسمی، در سال ۲۰۲۴، ۲۲ زن سعودی حق ثبت اختراع دریافت کردند و زنان سعودی ۱۹۵۶ جایزه داخلی و بین‌المللی در حوزه ورزش به دست آوردند.

این ارقام به این معنا نیست که تجربه زنان در سراسر عربستان یکسان است یا تحولات اجتماعی در همه‌ جا با سرعتی مشابه رخ داده است، اما نشان می‌دهد حوزه‌هایی که زنان سعودی در آن‌ها حضور دارند، از بازار کار و آموزش گرفته تا ورزش و فعالیت‌های تفریحی، گسترده‌تر شده است.

گسترش مشارکت زنان نیز لزوما به معنای تحقق برابری حقوقی و اجتماعی نیست.

دیده‌بان حقوق بشر در گزارش سال ۲۰۲۶ خود هشدار می‌دهد که اصلاحاتی که به‌عنوان نشانه‌های نوسازی معرفی می‌شوند، هم‌زمان با ادامه محدودیت‌های قانونی همراه‌اند.  برخی از این محدودیت‌های قانونی از طریق نظام احوال شخصیه، استقلال و حقوق زنان در موضوعاتی مانند ازدواج، طلاق و حضانت اعمال می‌شوند.

در اینجا باید میان محدودیت‌های قانونی و سنت‌های اجتماعی تفاوت قائل شد. زنان در عربستان سعودی هرگز به‌طور قانونی از موتورسواری منع نشده بودند؛ به همان شکلی که تا پیش از سال ۲۰۱۸ از رانندگی خودرو منع می‌شدند.

در سال ۲۰۱۷، خبرگزاری رسمی عربستان سعودی توضیح داد که مجوز رانندگی برای زنان شامل موتورسیکلت نیز می‌شود و مقررات نظام راهنمایی و رانندگی و آیین‌نامه‌های اجرایی آن برای زنان و مردان به یکسان اعمال می‌شود.

اما وجود یک حق قانونی «لزوما به این معنا نیست که انجام آن فعالیت یک‌شبه به امری عادی و پذیرفته‌شده در جامعه تبدیل شود». سم می‌گوید این دقیقاً یکی از چالش‌هایی بوده که با آن روبه‌رو شده است.

به گفته او، پذیرش حضور زنان موتور‌سوار در همه جا یکسان نیست و واکنش‌ها می‌تواند از فردی به فرد دیگر و از شهری به شهر دیگر متفاوت باشد.

با این حال، او معتقد است روند کلی در سال‌های اخیر مثبت‌تر شده و میزان حمایتی که زنان امروز دریافت می‌کنند، به‌مراتب بیشتر از گذشته است.

سم همچنین بر این باور است که حمایت برخی چهره‌های شناخته‌شده ورزشی به افزایش حضور و دیده‌شدن زنان در این عرصه کمک کرده است.

یکی از بزرگ‌ترین موانع پیش روی زنان در این حوزه، نبود محیطی آشنا و در دسترس برای آغاز این مسیر بوده است.

سم می‌گوید هزینه آموزش و تهیه تجهیزات ایمنی برای برخی افراد می‌تواند بالا باشد. علاوه بر این، زنی که وارد عرصه‌ای می‌شود که به طور سنتی در اختیار مردان بوده، ممکن است بارها ناچار شود توانایی‌های خود را ثابت کند. با این حال، او تاکید می‌کند که «اجازه ندادم نظرها و حرف‌های منفی انتخاب‌هایم را تعیین کنند.»

هدف او از ابتدا این بود که موتورسواری را به شکلی درست و ایمن یاد بگیرد و از طریق تمرین مداوم، اعتمادبه‌نفس خود را تقویت کند.

او می‌گوید مادرش، پیش از درگذشت، یکی از بزرگ‌ترین حامیانش بود: «به من افتخار می‌کرد و همیشه تشویقم می‌کرد زنی مستقل باشم که بتواند روی خودش حساب کند.»

درباره برادرانش نیز می‌گوید آنها در ابتدا با این ایده مخالف بودند، اما بعدها نظرشان تغییر کرد و حتی خودش آموزش موتورسواری به یکی از برادرانش را بر عهده گرفت.

سم معتقد است تجربه‌های فردی مانند تجربه او می‌توانند به مرور بخشی از تغییری بزرگ‌تر در نگاه زنان به خود و جایگاهشان در جامعه شوند. او می‌گوید مسیرش هنوز ادامه دارد و قصد ندارد فقط به آموزش موتورسواری بسنده کند. هدف او توسعه بیشتر مهارت‌هایش، شرکت در مسابقات موتورسواری و جلب حمایت نهادهای رسمی از ورزش زنان است.

او می‌گوید: «موتورسیکلت فقط یک وسیله نیست؛ احساسی از آزادی است. این داستانی است که هر روز می‌نویسم و راهی است برای رسیدن به خودِ واقعی‌ام.»

در شرایطی که حضور زنان در عربستان سعودی در حوزه‌هایی که پیش‌تر مشارکت کمتری در آنها داشتند رو به گسترش است، تجربه‌هایی از این دست نیز به‌تدریج از یک استثنای قابل توجه به بخشی از چشم‌انداز اجتماعی در حال تغییر این کشور تبدیل می‌شوند.

در خیابان‌های جده، جایی که رفت‌وآمد خودروها با ضرباهنگ شهری که به‌سرعت در حال دگرگونی است درهم می‌آمیزد، زنی جوان که در عربستان سعودی متولد و بزرگ شده، با موتورسیکلت خود مسیرش را باز می‌کند.

برای صدف محمد شریف، که خود را «سم» معرفی می‌کند، موتورسیکلت تنها یک سرگرمی یا راهی برای پر کردن اوقات فراغت نبوده، بلکه بخشی از سفری شخصی برای بازیابی اعتمادبه‌نفس و احساس استقلال بوده است.

این زن جوان که خود را از کودکی شیفته ماجراجویی توصیف می‌کند، می‌گوید آشنایی‌اش با موتورسیکلت در دوره‌ای دشوار از زندگی‌اش آغاز شد؛ زمانی که به گفته خودش «نیاز داشتم از خانه بیرون بیایم، تعادل پیدا کنم و خودم را دوباره به دست بیاورم.»

داستان سم در زمانی روایت می‌شود که زندگی زنان در عربستان سعودی شاهد دگرگونی‌های اجتماعی و اقتصادی شتابانی است؛ تحولاتی که در چند سال گذشته بیش از پیش آشکار شده‌اند.

اجازه رانندگی به زنان در ژوئن ۲۰۱۸ یکی از نمادین‌ترین تغییرات در این مسیر بود. پیش از آن، زنان در عربستان سعودی برای دهه‌ها اجازه رانندگی نداشتند.

بر اساس آمار سازمان کل آمار عربستان سعودی، بین ژوئن ۲۰۱۸ تا ژانویه ۲۰۲۰، در مجموع ۱۷۴ هزار و ۶۲۴ گواهینامه رانندگی برای زنان صادر شد.

دولت عربستان می‌گوید این تحول در چارچوب «چشم‌انداز ۲۰۳۰» قرار دارد که افزایش مشارکت زنان در بازار کار را یکی از اهداف خود تعیین کرده است.

مشارکت زنان سعودی در بازار کار از هدف اولیه ۳۰ درصدی چشم‌انداز عبور کرده و مقام‌ها را واداشته است هدف را به ۴۰ درصد تا سال ۲۰۳۰ افزایش دهند.

اما ارقام اقتصادی به‌ تنهایی همه داستان تغییر اجتماعی را روایت نمی‌کنند.

در زندگی روزمره، برخی زنان همچنان در حال آزمودن مرزهای تازه آن چیزی هستند که از نظر اجتماعی معمول تلقی می‌شود؛ چه در کار، ورزش، رفت‌وآمد یا دنبال کردن سرگرمی‌هایی که به‌طور سنتی با مردان مرتبط بوده‌اند.

تجربه سم در همین چارچوب قرار می‌گیرد.

سم می‌گوید در آغاز، مانند بسیاری از کسانی که برای نخستین بار موتورسیکلت‌سواری را امتحان می‌کنند، «ترسیده و مضطرب» بود.

او به بی‌بی‌سی عربی می‌گوید حتی نمی‌دانست چگونه تعادلش را حفظ کند.

مربی‌اش به او توصیه کرد ابتدا دوچرخه‌سواری یاد بگیرد و بعد به تمرین موتورسیکلت برگردد.

سم همین کار را کرد. ابتدا یاد گرفت چگونه تعادل بدنش را روی دوچرخه حفظ کند، سپس به موتورسیکلت برگشت، بر ترسش غلبه کرد و تعادل بیشتری پیدا کرد.

به گفته او، همین گام کوچک آغاز یک تحول بزرگ‌تر بود.

در شروع، احساس «تنها بودن» در محیط اطرافش همیشه همراهش بود. دیدن زنی که در خیابان‌های عربستان موتورسیکلت می‌راند هم صحنه‌ای معمول نبود، اما او تصمیم گرفت ادامه دهد.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

وقتی به پنج سال پیش برمی‌گردد، به یاد می‌آورد که چگونه با تحسین به موتورسواران نگاه می‌کرد؛ افرادی که برای او نماد قدرت و استواری بودند. موتورسیکلت‌های بزرگ، لباس‌های ایمنی و مهارت موتورسواران در کنترل وسیله‌ای سنگین و پرسرعت، او را مجذوب خود کرده بود.

می‌گوید: «می‌خواستم مثل آن‌ها باشم، قوی و مستقل.»

با گذشت زمان، این علاقه به تمرین مداوم و سپس به مهارتی حرفه‌ای تبدیل شد؛ مهارتی که به او امکان داد به مربی رسمی موتورسواری تبدیل شود.

بعدتر، سم همراه چند زن دیگر در جده یک گروه زنان موتورسوار با نام «دختران موتورسوار» راه‌اندازی کرد و از طریق شبکه‌های اجتماعی گروهش را معرفی کرد تا زنان بیشتری را به این ورزش ترغیب کند.

اعضای گروه در صفحه اینستاگرام خود، ویدئوهایی از سفرها و تمرین‌هایشان منتشر می‌کنند و به زنان جوان دیگری که می‌خواهند موتورسیکلت‌سواری یاد بگیرند اما نمی‌دانند از کجا شروع کنند یا از چه کسی راهنمایی بگیرند، مشورت می‌دهند.

تعداد اعضای جامعه زنان موتورسوار که سم بنیان گذاشته به حدود ۱۷۰ نفر رسیده است.

او می‌گوید: «دیگر یک گروه کوچک نیستیم، به شبکه‌ای تبدیل شده‌ایم که در آن از یکدیگر حمایت می‌کنیم.»

به گفته سم، تاکنون بیش از ۲۰۰ زن از طریق این گروه برای توسعه و بهبود مهارت‌های موتورسیکلت‌سواری خود حمایت و کمک دریافت کرده‌اند.

او می‌گوید بسیاری از اعضا بسیار فعال‌اند، به‌ویژه در تمرین منظم. آن‌ها بیشتر آخرهفته‌ها برای موتورسواری و شرکت در فعالیت‌ها و رویدادهای مختلف بیرون می‌روند، از جمله «تور اکتبر صورتی» و «تور روز ملی عربستان»، و همچنین مجموعه‌ای گسترده از برنامه‌های اجتماعی و رویدادهای موتورسیکلت‌سواری که در طول سال برگزار می‌شوند.

سم خود را تنها زن موتوسوار نمی‌داند، بلکه خود را بخشی از نسلی از زنان در عربستان می‌بیند که فضاهای تازه‌ای را در زندگی عمومی تجربه می‌کنند.

در شرایطی که حضور زنان در عربستان سعودی در حوزه‌هایی که پیش‌تر مشارکت کمتری در آنها داشتند رو به گسترش است، تجربه‌هایی از این دست نیز به‌تدریج از یک استثنای قابل توجه به بخشی از چشم‌انداز اجتماعی در حال تغییر این کشور تبدیل می‌شوند.

news.originalContent:
Photo by Imen Ben Youssef / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images

Nvidia quickly shut down the idea that former CEO Jensen Huang would be returning to the company after President Donald Trump made comments about hiring him back.

Trump on Monday told gathered media that having Huang back at the helm of the trillion dollar tech company “certainly isn’t a bad idea.” But just hours later, a source confirmed that Nvidia’s board of directors is in fact not considering bringing back the company’s longtime leader.

The Nvidia board is focused on wrapping up the internal independent investigation into Huang’s conduct at the company and working towards identifying a new permanent CEO, the a source familiar with the board’s deliberations who spoke with DCNF on the condition of anonymity said. (RELATED: Trump Casts Doubt On Chinese Spy Allegations Plaguing Nvidia, Calls For Ousted CEO To Return)

The company is conducting an ongoing investigation into Huang’s conduct and hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into whether Huang’s affairs compromised national security or company secrets, CNBC reported Monday.

Huang on Nov. 8 admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, the former CEO of Singaporean tech company Megaspeed, who some allege to be a Chinese spy. Ms. Huang, to whom the longtime former Nvidia CEO is not related, reportedly used her ties to him to help transport Nvidia chips worth at least a combined $7.5 billion to Chinese firms.

Huang seems to have amassed a steady following of supporters following his Thursday resignation. Over 185,600 signatories including shareholders, partners, Nvidia’s employees, and other supporters signed a letter demanding the board re-hire the 33-year CEO, according to an online campaign dubbed “Stand with Jensen.”

@yunta_tsai A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too

“Thirty-three years deserves an answer. We demand the Nvidia board bring Jensen back,” the campaign webpage says. “Thank you Jensen, we stand with you.”

Notable signers include trillionaire Elon Musk, who wrote on his platform X about his intention to sign Friday.

“The president’s comments DO matter,” Jim Cramer, the host of CNBC’s “Mad Money,” wrote in a Monday X post. “The president can do a pre-pardon, say that Jensen is a too important to Nvidia and Nvidia is a national treasure. That’s how it would go.”

The president’s comments DO matter. The president can do a pre-pardon, say that Jensen is a too important to Nvidia and Nvidia is a national treasure. That’s how it would go.

“If he can get through the legal trouble, I think we’ll have a second act from him,” Jay Goldberg, senior analyst for Seaport Research Partners told CNBC’s “Squawk Box Asia.”

However other Wall Street analysts denied this claim.

“We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO,” Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., said in a note, according to CNBC.

Federal investigators including lawmakers have also opened investigations into Huang’s affair implications on national security, CNBC reported Friday.

Colette Kress became Nvidia’s interim CEO following Huang’s resignation.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Kayla Bartkowski/Getty Images)

Republican Florida Rep. Maria Salazar sent an email Monday celebrating that her amnesty bill garnered more supporters.

The DIGNIDAD (Dignity Act) would grant a legal pathway to citizenship for illegal aliens already in the U.S., secure the border, end illegal immigration and reform the asylum system to make it more efficient. Salazar, who introduced the legislation, accused President Donald Trump’s immigration policies of having gone “too far” in a campaign advertisement from September.

The legislation gained 16 new co-sponsors as of Monday, bringing the number of co-sponsors up to 55.

Twenty Republicans, including Reps. Mike Lawler of New York, Dan Newhouse of Washington, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Monica De La Cruz of Texas and Don Bacon of Nebraska were among the Republicans to co-sponsor the pro-amnesty legislation. Republican Florida Rep. Carlos Gimenez and Democratic Reps. Angie Craig of Minnesota, Seth Moulton of Massachusetts, Josh Gottheimer of New Jersey and Chris Pappas of New Hampshire were among the 16 new co-sponsors.

“Sixteen more Members of Congress are joining an effort that has been growing all year, both on Capitol Hill and across the country. This proves that Republicans and Democrats can still come together to find a solution to America’s immigration crisis,” Salazar said. “We are building a coalition around a simple principle: America can have law and order, economic prosperity, and human dignity. We do not have to choose. The legislation is written, the support is growing, and now Congress has an opportunity to turn that progress into law.” (RELATED: Zombie Amnesty Plan Shambles On In Lame Duck Congress Amid Trump Floating Deal With Democrats)

Salazar said in the September campaign ad that Hispanics felt “betrayed” by Trump’s deportation policies.

“In July, 50% of the 50,000 people that were detained had no criminal record,” Salazar said. “Be careful what your advisers are telling you about immigration policy. The same Hispanics who helped you get to the White House in 2024 feel betrayed today. You can be for immigration what Lincoln was for slavery and Reagan was for communism.”

Republican Texas Rep. Brandon Gill argued the legislation would be a “terrible betrayal” to Republican voters.

“The Dignity Act is mass amnesty and would constitute a terrible betrayal to our voters,” Gill said in an April 7 X post.

Salazar denied that the bill provided amnesty to illegal immigrants.

“READ. THE. BILL. BEFORE. YOU. OPEN. YOUR. MOUTH,” Salazar responded. “Calling the DIGNITY Act ‘amnesty’ isn’t just wrong. It’s a deliberate distortion and it exposes just how little you know about the bill. This is enforcement first: zero tolerance for criminals, permanent border security, and hard, earned requirements to step forward and face the law, so American workers are protected, not undercut. Amnesty is the chaos you’ve defended, millions in the shadows, no control, no accountability, and a system that stopped working a long time ago.”

Maria, your ‘DIGNIDAD Act’ would give legal status to over 10 million illegal aliens. It’s rank amnesty and everybody knows it. I want dignity for Americans - the people whose interests we represent - not illegal aliens. That means doing what we said we’d do: mass deportations.

Gill argued that handing legal status to 10 million illegal aliens is amnesty.

“Maria, your ‘DIGNIDAD Act’ would give legal status to over 10 million illegal aliens,” Gill said. “It’s rank amnesty and everybody knows it. I want dignity for Americans - the people whose interests we represent - not illegal aliens. That means doing what we said we’d do: mass deportations.”

Members of the House Freedom Caucus, including Republican Texas Rep. Chip Roy, argued that the bill rewarded illegal immigration.

Over 100 national organizations and the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus endorsed the bill. Among these organizations were the American Latino Coalition, Migrants Foundation Inc., the Anti-Defamation League and the National Immigration Forum.

Voters identified immigration as one of their top issues during the 2024 election, helping Trump win re-election. While Hispanic voters voted for Democrats over Republicans during the 2026 midterms, sixty-one percent of voters identifying immigration as their top issue voted Republican.

Most Hispanic voters were more concerned about the economy than immigration, prompting them to vote Democrat, according to an NBC News exit poll.

Trump campaigned against granting amnesty to illegal aliens. He said during a Nov. 8 interview on “60 Minutes” that his deportation policies may have been “too tough.”

Trump endorsed Salazar ahead of her primary in August, arguing she had been “doing a truly fantastic job.” Salazar narrowly won re-election by a 50.2% to 49.8% margin, The Associated Press reported Tuesday. Her Miami-area district is 73.5% Hispanic, according to Legisletter.

Salazar was one of the few Republicans who voted with Democrats to create a committee to investigate Jan. 6.

news.originalContent:
(Getty Images/Harry Durrant)

The Israeli military reportedly uploaded millions of photographs of Palestinians to Amazon’s artificial intelligence platform as part of an expansive surveillance operation in Gaza and the West Bank.

Israeli military officials transferred approximately 3.5 million photographs to Amazon Web Services (AWS) in early 2024 to use the company’s AI-powered facial recognition technology, according to leaked documents obtained by The Guardian. The operation was conducted by an Israeli military department known as Rolling Stone, which maintains extensive databases of Palestinians’ personal information, as the military expanded its use of facial recognition technology to identify individuals at checkpoints and track suspected militants.

The Israeli Foreign Ministry and AWS did not immediately reply to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment. (RELATED: Trump Admin Bars Visa For Priest Seeking To Expose Plight Of Palestinian Christians)

Israel’s military uploaded 3.5 million photos to Amazon’s cloud platform to use its facial recognition technology to surveil Palestinians https://t.co/a8JnbKietQ https://t.co/0UDb3ynVTS

Amazon in 2021 executed a deal with the Israeli government known as Project Nimbus. Under that multibillion dollar contract, AWS and Google provide cloud services to a multitude of military and government clients.

The contract with Israel includes unusual terms that prohibit either company from suspending or terminating Israeli military or government use of their cloud database, even if Israel breaches the terms of service, a previous Guardian investigation indicated.

As part of the deal, AWS opened new datacenters in Israel in 2024. Around this time, a small group of Israeli soldiers known as Rolling Stone began working out of the AWS office in Tel Aviv. This group was developing ways to use AWS cloud infrastructure to more effectively operate a facial recognition program in Gaza that was rolled out after the Oct. 7, 2023 attacks called Rekognition. It is unclear if this work was related to the 3.5 million images uploaded.

“Any suggestion that these visits are anything other than routine customer engagement is wrong and unsubstantiated,” an AWS spokesperson told the Guardian.

Previously, the Israeli military experimented with facial recognition in Gaza. However, the program was faulty and led to civilians being targeted as militants, the New York Times reported in March 2024.

«از همه کسانی که در استودیوهای آمازون ام‌جی‌ام به من اعتماد کردند، صمیمانه سپاسگزارم. گفتن اینکه این نقش، رویایی است که به حقیقت پیوسته است، حق مطلب را ادا نمی‌کند. بی‌اندازه برای این همکاری و کاری که با این تیم فوق‌العاده پیش رو داریم، هیجان‌زده‌ام.»

پتینسون ۴۰ ساله با بازی در نقش ادوارد کالن در مجموعه فیلم حماسه گرگ‌ومیش شهرتی جهانی پیدا کرد. او در فیلم تنت به کارگردانی کریستوفر نولان نیز نقش یک جاسوس را بازی کرده بود و مدتی قبل هم فیلم اودیسه، دیگر همکاری این دو نفر روی پرده سینماها رفت.

رابرت پتینسون همچنین پس از سه فیلم بتمن به کارگردانی نولان که کریستین بیل نقش اول را بازی می‌کرد، در فیلم بتمن (۲۰۲۲) ساخته مت ریوز نقش این ابرقهرمان را بازی کرد و قرار است در ادامه هم چنین نقشی را اجرا کند. به این ترتیب، برای اولین بار در تاریخ سینما بازیگر بتمن و جیمز باند یک نفر خواهد بود.

دنی ویلنوو، کارگردان فیلم بعدی جیمز باند، نیز درباره انتخاب این بازیگر گفت: «پیش از هر چیز، می‌خواهم از بازیگران فوق‌العاده‌ای که در این مسیر همراهمان شدند، صمیمانه تشکر کنم. استعدادهای بی‌نظیری دور ما بودند، اما فقط یک نفر می‌تواند ۰۰۷ باشد.»

«از اینکه به رابرت پتینسون به‌عنوان جیمز باند تازه‌مان خوشامد می‌گوییم، از ته دل خوشحالم. او روح همیشگی ۰۰۷ را دارد و حال‌وهوایی کاملا تازه با خودش می‌آورد. برای شروع کار لحظه‌شماری می‌کنم.»

ایمی پاسکال و دیوید هیمن، دو تهیه‌کننده سرشناس فیلم بعدی جیمز باند، می‌گویند که با حضور رابرت پتینسون «میراث این شخصیت به دست آدم درستی سپرده شده است».

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

این دو در بیانیه‌ای مشترک گفتند: «جیمز باند یکی از محبوب‌ترین و الهام‌بخش‌ترین و ماندگارترین شخصیت‌های ادبیات و سینماست و در عین حال، هنوز رازآلود مانده است.»

«میراث این شخصیت به دست آدم درستی سپرده شده است. جسارت او در بازیگری، شوخ‌طبعی‌اش در دست انداختن خودش، و توانایی‌اش در اینکه مدام خودش را از نو بسازد، او را به باندی بی‌نقص برای روزگار ما تبدیل می‌کند.»

پاسکال تهیه‌کننده فیلم‌هایی از جمله «شکارچیان روح» و «زنان کوچک» و «مرد عنکبوتی: به درون دنیای عنکبوتی» بوده است و برای همین فیلم آخر در سال ۲۰۱۹ جایزه گلدن گلوب را برده است.

هیمن از سال ۱۹۹۲ در صنعت سینما فعالیت می‌کند و ۱۲ جایزه برده است که بیشترشان برای کارهایش در مجموعه فیلم‌های «هری پاتر» و «پدینگتون» بوده است.

پیش از این فقط شش بازیکن در نقش این ابرجاسوس بریتانیایی بازی کرده‌اند:

انتظار می‌رود تولید این فیلم سال ۲۰۲۷ آغاز شود و سال ۲۰۲۸ اکران شود. هنوز تاریخ دقیقی اعلام نشده است. برنامه‌های فیلمسازی معمولا بسیار تغییرپذیرند اما روشن است که کار ساخت این فیلم حسابی پیش رفته است و کارگردان و نویسنده آن مشخص شده‌اند.

این بیست‌وششمین فیلم مجموعه رسمی باند خواهد بود ولی نام آن هنوز تایید نشده است.

news.originalContent:
هفته گذشته وقتی بی‌بی‌سی ویدئویی از روشن شدن چراغ‌های کریسمس در خیابان کارنابی لندن منتشر کرد، بخش نظرهای آن پر شد از واکنش هزاران نفر به چیزی که دیده بودند.

واکنش کاربران، نه به چراغ‌های درخشان و نه به آتش‌بازی زیبا که به دریای تماشاگرانی بود که با گوشی‌هایشان فیلم می‌گرفتند.

یکی نوشته بود: «یادتان هست وقتی چیزها را مستقیم با چشم خودمان نگاه می‌کردیم؟ چه روزگار خوشی بود.» دیگری فقط نوشته بود: «چه صحنه غم‌انگیزی، واقعا غم‌انگیز.»

ناتالی کسیدی، بازیگر پیشین سریال ایست‌اندرز، نوشت: «چرا این گزارش به این موضوع اشاره نمی‌کند که هیچ‌کس این نمایش زیبا را با چشم خودش نگاه نمی‌کند؟ واقعا ترسناک و ناامیدکننده است.»

بسیاری در نظرهایشان پرسیده بودند چرا آدم‌ها به جای این که آتش‌بازی را با چشم خودشان ببینند، از آن فیلم می‌گیرند. یکی نوشته بود: «چه خوب که همه در لحظه زندگی می‌کنند. ۹۰ درصد احتمال دارد هیچ‌وقت هم دوباره این ویدئو را تماشا نکنند.»

از زمانی که تقریبا گوشی همه، دوربین دارد، پژوهش‌های متعددی انجام شده تا مشخص شود که ثبت رویدادها با عکس یا فیلم چه اثری بر حافظه ما می‌گذارد.

بسیاری از این پژوهش‌ها به این نتیجه رسیده‌اند که عکس یا فیلم گرفتن از چیزی، نه تنها به ما کمک نمی‌کند آن لحظه را به خاطر بسپاریم، بلکه در واقع ممکن است مانع شود آن را دقیق به یاد بیاوریم.

دانشمندان اسم این پدیده را «آسیب ناشی از عکس گرفتن» گذاشته‌اند؛ اصطلاحی که نخستین بار دکتر لیندا هنکل، روان‌شناس، در سال ۲۰۱۴ و در جریان پژوهش درباره این موضوع به کار برد.

پژوهش‌ها و آزمایش‌هایی که بعدها درباره حافظه انجام شد، بارها نشان داده که انسان‌ها ناخودآگاه کار به خاطر سپردن را به دوربین می‌سپارند و دیگر مغزشان را برای به یاد سپردن رویدادها در همان لحظه‌ای که اتفاق می‌افتند، به کار نمی‌گیرند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

برای دکتر کیتلین رگر از دانشگاه کالج لندن، نکته جالب این ماجرا آن همه آدمی نیست که فیلم می‌گیرند، بلکه کسانی است که در فضای مجازی از این موضوع عصبانی‌اند: «امسال اولین سالی نیست که آدم‌ها به مراسمی می‌روند و آن را از پشت صفحه نمایش تماشا می‌کنند اما نکته مهم این است که امسال بحث‌های انتقادی زیادی در افکار عمومی شکل گرفته است. به نظرم این واقعا، اتفاقی مثبت است.»

به گفته این استاد دانشگاه، نظرهایی مثل آنچه زیر ویدئوی خیابان کارنابی نوشته شده، «چیزهای زیادی درباره جایگاه کنونی ما به‌عنوان یک جامعه می‌گوید» و نشان‌دهنده «ناخشنودی ما از میزان نفوذی است که شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری بر زندگی‌مان دارند.»

خانم رگر می‌گوید که این تغییر نگرش نسبت به گوشی‌ها و فیلم گرفتن از رویدادها دلایل مختلفی دارد؛ از جمله ممنوعیت استفاده از شبکه‌های اجتماعی برای افراد زیر ۱۶ سال در بریتانیا که قرار است از مارس ۲۰۲۷ اجرا شود و همچنین شکایت‌هایی در آمریکا که از شرکت‌های شبکه‌های اجتماعی مطرح شده است.

به گفته او، این خبرهای منفی‌تر «درک عمومی» را بالا برده و مردم را تشویق می‌کند که «بخواهند کنترل بیشتری بر این فناوری‌ها داشته باشند.»

کیتلین رگر گفت که شاید «موج انتقادها» از ویدئوی خیابان کارنابی به این دلیل باشد که پای کریسمس در میان است و مردم به‌شدت معتقدند که کریسمس را نباید از پشت گوشی تجربه کرد: «ما، به‌عنوان پدر و مادرهای نسل هزاره، کریسمس‌های پیش از گوشی‌های هوشمند را به یاد داریم.»

«تصورات خیلی عمیقی از معنای آن روزها برای خودمان داریم و فکر می‌کنم آدم‌ها روزبه‌روز بیشتر از این ناراحت می‌شوند که بچه‌هایشان همان تجربه‌ها را ندارند، یا از این که فناوری میان بچه‌هایشان و این تجربه‌ها فاصله انداخته است. پدر و مادرها حالا واقعا از سلطه‌ای که فناوری بر زندگی خانواده‌شان پیدا کرده، ناراحت شده‌اند.»

بسیاری از این پژوهش‌ها به این نتیجه رسیده‌اند که عکس یا فیلم گرفتن از چیزی، نه تنها به ما کمک نمی‌کند آن لحظه را به خاطر بسپاریم، بلکه در واقع ممکن است مانع شود آن را دقیق به یاد بیاوریم.

دانشمندان اسم این پدیده را «آسیب ناشی از عکس گرفتن» گذاشته‌اند؛ اصطلاحی که نخستین بار دکتر لیندا هنکل، روان‌شناس، در سال ۲۰۱۴ و در جریان پژوهش درباره این موضوع به کار برد.

پژوهش‌ها و آزمایش‌هایی که بعدها درباره حافظه انجام شد، بارها نشان داده که انسان‌ها ناخودآگاه کار به خاطر سپردن را به دوربین می‌سپارند و دیگر مغزشان را برای به یاد سپردن رویدادها در همان لحظه‌ای که اتفاق می‌افتند، به کار نمی‌گیرند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

برای دکتر کیتلین رگر از دانشگاه کالج لندن، نکته جالب این ماجرا آن همه آدمی نیست که فیلم می‌گیرند، بلکه کسانی است که در فضای مجازی از این موضوع عصبانی‌اند: «امسال اولین سالی نیست که آدم‌ها به مراسمی می‌روند و آن را از پشت صفحه نمایش تماشا می‌کنند اما نکته مهم این است که امسال بحث‌های انتقادی زیادی در افکار عمومی شکل گرفته است. به نظرم این واقعا، اتفاقی مثبت است.»

به گفته این استاد دانشگاه، نظرهایی مثل آنچه زیر ویدئوی خیابان کارنابی نوشته شده، «چیزهای زیادی درباره جایگاه کنونی ما به‌عنوان یک جامعه می‌گوید» و نشان‌دهنده «ناخشنودی ما از میزان نفوذی است که شرکت‌های بزرگ فناوری بر زندگی‌مان دارند.»

خانم رگر می‌گوید که این تغییر نگرش نسبت به گوشی‌ها و فیلم گرفتن از رویدادها دلایل مختلفی دارد؛ از جمله ممنوعیت استفاده از شبکه‌های اجتماعی برای افراد زیر ۱۶ سال در بریتانیا که قرار است از مارس ۲۰۲۷ اجرا شود و همچنین شکایت‌هایی در آمریکا که از شرکت‌های شبکه‌های اجتماعی مطرح شده است.

به گفته او، این خبرهای منفی‌تر «درک عمومی» را بالا برده و مردم را تشویق می‌کند که «بخواهند کنترل بیشتری بر این فناوری‌ها داشته باشند.»

کیتلین رگر گفت که شاید «موج انتقادها» از ویدئوی خیابان کارنابی به این دلیل باشد که پای کریسمس در میان است و مردم به‌شدت معتقدند که کریسمس را نباید از پشت گوشی تجربه کرد: «ما، به‌عنوان پدر و مادرهای نسل هزاره، کریسمس‌های پیش از گوشی‌های هوشمند را به یاد داریم.»

«تصورات خیلی عمیقی از معنای آن روزها برای خودمان داریم و فکر می‌کنم آدم‌ها روزبه‌روز بیشتر از این ناراحت می‌شوند که بچه‌هایشان همان تجربه‌ها را ندارند، یا از این که فناوری میان بچه‌هایشان و این تجربه‌ها فاصله انداخته است. پدر و مادرها حالا واقعا از سلطه‌ای که فناوری بر زندگی خانواده‌شان پیدا کرده، ناراحت شده‌اند.»

Rex Ryan crushed the Cowboys’ defense in a rant on ESPN New York Monday morning, with the former Jets coach claiming that he could turn Dallas’ unit around in one week.

The bravado-filled statement came a day after the Cowboys lost to the 49ers despite scoring 40 points, as the defense allowed nearly 600 yards for a 46-40 loss in another disappointing day for the franchise.

It also came less than a week after Ryan was arrested for an alleged incident in which he ran over two people’s feet on a Nashville street and fled the scene in his pickup truck.

Ryan resumed his regularly scheduled media appearances over the weekend despite the legal issues and had no problem criticizing the Cowboys on Monday on the radio.

“It’s the worst-coached defense I’ve ever seen,” Ryan said of the Cowboys unit led by coordinator Christian Parker. “It really is. And I’ve seen some horrible defenses, this one’s awful, and it starts with coaching. … They make more mental mistakes than any defense I’ve seen, as well as the physical, they’re not a tough physical defense.”

Ryan was credited with having some of the best defenses in the NFL during his run with the Jets, especially in his first two years, when he coached the Jets to back-to-back appearances in the AFC title game.

Ryan has also never been shy about the confidence he has in himself, leading to a bold statement while speaking with Rick DiPietro and Dave Rothenberg on his weekly spot on their show.

“I could go there today and say, ‘All right, we can have an average ass defense.’ I’ll promise you they’d be average, I’d probably make them top 10,” Ryan boasted. “But I’ll take that group right now, in one week, I’d go in and turn this thing out. Instead, they’re going to play this and have no freaking clue. They gave up 584 yards in this game [against the 49ers]. We got issues with the Jets, we do, but are you kidding me?

“I don’t think anybody thought the Jets were going to make the Super Bowl and this team comes in there, you scored 40 points and got beat by six. It’s unreal, man.”

Ryan appeared on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown” as an analyst just days after his arrest and has not publicly addressed the allegations.

The alleged incident occurred on Nov. 5 when two people claim Ryan hit them with his vehicle as they were crossing the street and had a walk signal.

Ryan is facing six misdemeanor charges and is due back in court for a hearing on Dec. 18.

There’s an insidious problem surrounding the NBA.

We’ve all heard of “shut up and dribble,” but what about “shut up and look pretty?”

It’s a sentiment surrounding players’ wives that has become glaring in the aftermath of the drama around Ayesha Curry, the wife of two-time MVP and four-time NBA champion Steph Curry.

Ayesha kissed Matthew Daddario while acting in “Second Chance Holiday,” which premiered on the Roku channel on Thursday.

That stunned many of Curry’s fans, including former NBA players Nick Young and Gilbert Arenas, who proceeded to discuss the matter on the podcast, “We Said What We Said.”

“The only blemish in the family is the wife in the sense because she doesn’t act like the other superstars’ wives,” Arenas said. “[Michael] Jordan’s wife, Cookie [Johnson], that’s Magic’s [Johnson’s] wife, Savannah [James], right, where we don’t want to hear you.”

Arenas poured more gasoline on the fire.

“We want it to be a problem because Steph is so innocent,” he added.

The kiss was also discussed by former NFL player Emmanuel Acho on the Speakeasy podcast. He said he wouldn’t tolerate his partner kissing another man while acting. “It wouldn’t be me,” he said, “It couldn’t be me.”

Added Acho: “…People are just going to use this as a reason to clown Steph. Don’t let your significant other be the reason that you get clowned.”

Steph, who typically doesn’t get involved in the fray, felt a need to respond to the criticism surrounding Ayesha, who has acted in multiple films, including “Irish Wish” and “Joy to the World,” and the TV show “Hannah Montana.”

Steph called out Arenas, Young and Acho, as well as anyone else who feels the need to “give an opinion on something you really don’t know about.”

Curry said they were trying to “step on the accomplishments of my wife,” adding that it “speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they’re allowed and what they’re not allowed to do.” He also said they were ignorant to “how acting works.”

“Obviously, I tried to laugh this off,” Steph said. “But something needs to be said.”

What happened next showed that Steph’s point was lost.

While each of those three men issued apologies, none of them were directed towards Ayesha. They were all aimed at Steph. There was something really off the mark about that.

Said Young: “I’m sorry Steph. You my dog, I love you. If I say anything, I apologize like a man.”

Added Arenas: “I’m sorry if he’s offended. I didn’t mean it like that. I was just saying that he’s such a perfect dude… but I am sorry.”

Said Acho: “Steph, I’m sorry, not just for offending you, potentially offending your wife.”

It’s clear that NBA players’ wives are supposed to be seen, not heard. They’re accessories, not people.

Steph and Ayesha have been married since 2011. They have three children. They appear to have a very strong marriage.

Yet whenever Ayesha steps outside the lines of what is deemed acceptable for an NBA player’s wife to say or do, there’s seemingly a mob of indignant internet trolls and pundits who are lying in wait to misguidedly “stand up” for Steph.

This wasn’t the first time the hammer came down on Ayesha.

In an appearance on Jada Pinkett Smith’s talk show “Red Table Talk” in 2019, Ayesha acknowledged feeling insecure that she gets “zero” male attention while seeing women constantly throw themselves at her husband.

Again, the internet was incensed. Pundits were up in arms.

But you know who else was on that podcast? Steph’s own mother, Sonya, who was formerly married to NBA player Dell Curry and seemingly identified with Ayesha’s point by comforting her, saying, “You’re not looking.”

Ayesha also received a ton of backlash after opening up about her career ambitions in an appearance on the podcast “Call Her Daddy” in August 2025.

When asked if she always wanted a big family, she responded earnestly.

“No,” she said. “So, I didn’t want kids. I didn’t want to get married. I thought I was going to be a career girl and that’s it. And I had my eyes set on my goals, and I was never the little girl that, like, dreamt about the wedding dress and all of that, and then it happened so early in my life.”

Ayesha went on to make it clear that she has no regrets.

“I wouldn’t change a thing, of course,” she added.

But still the outside noise became deafening, with her detractors uttering different forms of the same sentiment.

She’s ungrateful. How dare she say those things. Poor Steph.

Is an NBA player’s wife not allowed to become an actress? Have insecurities? Career ambitions?

You know who stood by her through all of this?

Steph, the very person whom the angry mobs were purporting to defend.

It’s pervasive. It’s obvious. It’s misogynistic.

It can be summed up in five words.

“Shut up and look pretty.”

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Popular Instagram account Overheard LA, which boasts 1.5 million followers, sparked a heated debate after sharing one woman’s frustrating experience with a Hinge match who claimed to live in Long Beach, but actually resided in Orange County.

“I’ve tried to express that driving an hour for drinks is not something I’m interested in doing but given the initial connection I’m getting mixed reactions from friends of whether I should still try to go on the date with him,” she wrote.

“Am I the asshole for not wanting to date someone who lives in OC? Also why did he put he lives in Long Beach???”

Overheard LA quickly turned the dating dilemma into a public trial, asking its followers to weigh in on what it called a “Hinge radius crime.” And the jury wasn’t particularly sympathetic to the accused fisherman.

“Straight to jail for lying about location,” one person commented. “I DO NOT date outside my radius and I don’t date liars. Even if we hit it off he lives too far away and I’m not effing commuting for the D. Not sorry.”

The post racked up more than 3,800 likes and hundreds of comments, with fed-up Angelenos sharing their own horror stories of geographically undesirable matches.

“I’m married and live in Los Angeles, but if I was on the dating apps my radius would be 5 miles MAX,” another wrote.

Others questioned why the woman was expected to accommodate her match’s preferred location in the first place.

“If he wants to see her he should drive up to Culver,” one user noted.

“I’m just wondering why SHE is supposed to drive to be closer to him?” another asked.

As the debate continued on, Overheard LA shared a dramatic update from the woman at the center of the controversy, and it appeared the would-be Romeo only dug himself into a deeper hole.

“I reiterated 3 times that I need to meet in LA and he then proceeded to ask if I wanted to go do karaoke in Huntington Beach (diabolical for a first date) on 2 days I’d already told him I couldn’t do,” she wrote.

The repeated invitations to Orange County, despite her objections, ultimately proved too much. For the anonymous singleton, the verdict was clear: no date, no karaoke and definitely no hourlong drive down the 405.

news.originalContent:

A one-man homeless camp sprawling outside City Hall had moved again Monday — relocating just yards away as its lone resident toys with the Mamdani administration’s homeless policies.

Mark Roggemann, 50, moved his fiefdom of plants, mattresses, chairs and other items a mere dozen-or-so yards down Chambers St. after the Department of Homeless Services (DHS) ordered he abandon his old roosting spot on Sunday.

Now rather than being directly next door to City Hall, he’s just a little bit less directly next door to City Hall — and could be able to stay for at least the next seven days until the DHS orders him out again.

And it’s the second time he’s pulled the stunt in recent weeks.

On Thursday he moved his camp another couple yards away after the DHS completed a weeklong outreach period instituted under Mayor Zohran Mamdani that requires social workers to try to make outreach with residents of a homeless encampment and wait seven days before authorities are allowed to sweep camps out.

The stunt was also no surprise — Roggemann admitted he was deliberately shifting his camp yards at a time to reset the DHS’ clock, telling The Post after his last move that he was going to keep moving back and forth until somebody figured out how to fully oust him under the administration’s own rules.

That means for the last seven weeks, New Yorkers, tourists and the mayor himself have seen Roggemann’s enormous setup — measuring some 200-square feet once fully established — as they walk through City Hall Park in one of the Big Apple’s most iconic squares.

Roggemann isn’t the only one to take advantage of the mayor’s policies and his mandatory pre-sweep “engagement process.”

In September, a homeless encampment near NYU dorms was swept up after the weeklong process and finally being ordered to vacate — only for it to pop up again about 100 yards down the sidewalk.

The policy has also allowed encampments to flourish citywide — with one stretching some 12 blocks along 11th Avenue over the summer, while another this fall made its home in a historic pavilion around the corner from City Hall in Columbus Park.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Flying taxis could be buzzing over Los Angeles within weeks.

Archer Aviation plans to begin testing its futuristic Midnight aircraft at Hawthorne Airport within weeks, as it races to launch a passenger service in time for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The electric aircrafts won’t initially carry passengers, and they’ll be taking off from a conventional runway rather than lifting straight into the sky.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

“Within the next couple of weeks, people will start to see Midnight flying overhead in LA as they’re stuck in traffic,” Archer founder and CEO Adam Goldstein said.

The company has already been named the “official air taxi provider” for the Olympics by LA28, the committee organizing the Games.

But whether ordinary Angelenos will get to skip the gridlock remains an open question, with experts warning flights could be limited and fares could reach $500 or more per passenger.

Archer’s Midnight aircraft runs on electricity and uses multiple rotors designed to allow them to take off and land vertically, eliminating the need for traditional runways. The upcoming flights will give Archer an opportunity to demonstrate the aircraft’s capabilities and gain experience operating in LA’s busy airspace ahead of the Games.

“Los Angeles is where we are writing the blueprint for every city that follows,” Goldstein said during a Nov. 9 call with investors.

He said Archer plans to begin carrying non-paying passengers on demonstration flights in 2027.

But whether the company will be ready to transport Olympic spectators in 2028 remains uncertain, with several regulatory and logistical obstacles still standing in its way.

Among the biggest is securing Federal Aviation Administration approval confirming Midnight meets the safety and design standards required to carry paying passengers.

Archer has spent years laying the groundwork for its Los Angeles operations: In 2025, the company acquired control of the master lease at Hawthorne Airport, where construction is now underway on 11 new hangars.

Its longer-term plans include transporting passengers between major Olympic venues, including SoFi Stadium and the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. To make that possible, the company would need to establish a network of specialized landing facilities, known as “vertiports,” where electric aircraft could take off and land vertically.

In August, Archer announced plans to develop one of those facilities at L.A. Live in downtown Los Angeles, which will host several Olympic and Paralympic competitions. However, the project remains in the planning stages, with Archer and AEG, the company that operates L.A. Live, still evaluating how the facility would function and accommodate passengers, according to LAist.

It also remains unclear what local zoning permits would be required before the project could move forward.

And despite the company’s ambitious plans, its upcoming flights will not yet demonstrate all of Midnight’s intended capabilities.

Aerospace consultant Adrian Norris told LAist the aircraft will initially take off using a conventional runway at Hawthorne Airport rather than lifting vertically into the air.

He also questioned the significance of Archer’s recent authorization to conduct experimental flights, explaining such approvals are commonly used to demonstrate aircrafts to investors, potential customers and the media.

Goldstein, however, has portrayed the Los Angeles flights as a major breakthrough for the company.

“This is undoubtedly our most important commercialization milestone to date,” he said Monday.

Even if Archer receives the necessary federal approvals before the Olympics, aviation experts say the Games will likely serve as an opportunity to introduce the technology to a limited number of passengers rather than launch a widely available transportation service.

And the price of flying above LA’s traffic could be as breathtaking as the views.

Jaafar El-Awady, a mechanical engineering professor at Johns Hopkins University, estimated a one-way trip could cost between $150 and $500 or more per passenger, according to LAist.

Such fares could put the service out of reach for many Angelenos, turning the flying taxis into a luxury alternative to driving rather than an everyday transportation option.

The California Post reached out to Archer for more information about its plans but did not immediately hear back.

If it feels like the entire internet is in limbo right now — with major outages from Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase bank and United Airlines in the span of a few days — that’s because it is, cyber security experts say.

And it’s probably going to get worse before it gets better.

Major companies that underpin the entire digital economy are in a mad rush

Major companies that underpin the entire digital economy are in a mad rush
news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

If it feels like the entire internet is in limbo right now — with major outages from Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase bank and United Airlines in the span of a few days — that’s because it is, cyber security experts say.

And it’s probably going to get worse before it gets better.

Major companies that underpin the entire digital economy are in a mad rush to update their complicated and often outdated computer systems as AI tools come online.

There’s also a deadline to get this done before the holiday rush, when spending swells and more back-office employees take time off.

“It’s holiday time, it’s travel time, it’s shopping. So you have all those higher spikes in volume, and more pressure to [update your systems,]” Marva Bailer, CEO of tech advisory firm Qualaix, told The Post.

Legacy systems are looking increasingly like Frankenstein’s monster, with bolted-on parts from AI companies and third-party vendors offering more points of failure, she said.

That appears to be exactly what happened with Monday’s outage at Chase. The bank said a software bug within its systems caused a failure — but it also impacted related transactions with Zelle, Bank of America, Capital One, Wells Fargo, according to multiple reports.

Also on Monday, United Airlines was forced to halt all departing flights thanks to a technical problem with its system.

It came after Microsoft’s global outage on Thursday — which knocked out business software like Outlook email systems. The company said a “latent” software defect, combined with surging demand for servers, caused a cascade of failures.

Then, on Friday the FAA ordered a nationwide ground-stop that left thousands stranded at airports. That has been blamed on a malfunctioning router in the middle of Arkansas that overloaded servers on the agency’s aging system.

None of these incidents has been attributed to a cyber attack and the fears that AI could find and exploit new security flaws.

But, AI could still be partly to blame, said Bailer. Along with the holidays.Companies often freeze software changes during major shopping events such as Black Friday, creating a deadline for completing upgrades.The FAA and airlines would be under similar pressure as travelers prepare to crisscross the nation en masse.

Meanwhile, AI is allowing companies to identify software vulnerabilities at a much faster clip — potentially leaving IT workers with more problems to fix.

Complicating matters is an army of behind-the-scenes middlemen that most Americans don’t see, but rely on every time they swipe a debit card, book a flight, or send a payment.These third-party tech giants provide much of the technological muscle behind the banking industry.

“They do the billing. They do the encryption. They actually move the money,” Bailer said.“We’ve added layers,” she added.

“When we think about a banking system in layers, we think about branches and ATMs, but do we really think about Zelle?”

A faulty software patch or security update could potentially prevent otherwise functioning computer systems from communicating with one another — grinding the gears across the industry.

And the consequences of another meltdown during the holiday shopping frenzy could be particularly devastating for retailers.

“It’s not just consumers,” Bailer said. “It’s small businesses.”

Chase has not disclosed whether a software update triggered Monday’s outage. There is no evidence that the three incidents were connected or that AI was responsible.With Post wires.

news.originalSummary:
Trump departs for ASEAN on summit with Xi and Putin

Donald Trump is heading to the Philippines where he’s scheduled to speak at a meeting of ASEAN leaders in Manila. He then leaves for Shenzhen in China where he’ll meet Russia’s Vladimir Putin and China’s Xi Jinping for a three-way summit. Alan Fisher reports from Washington DC.
