news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

The race for the tiniest waist just got even more competitive.

New clinical trial results suggest a Chinese-made weight-loss drug could help people shed nearly 18% of their body weight in under a year.

The findings suggest the newcomer could one day outperform some of the biggest names in the booming GLP-1 market, including Wegovy and Mounjaro.

In the 48-week trial, researchers from Fudan University in Shanghai recruited 567 adults who were overweight or obese and divided them into four groups.

Three groups received weekly injections of ribupatide at doses of 2 milligrams, 4 milligrams or 6 milligrams, while the fourth received a placebo.

Behind the experimental drug is Chinese pharmaceutical giant Hengrui, which partnered with US biotech firm Kailera Therapeutics to bring ribupatide to markets outside China.

Ribupatide works by mimicking two hormones naturally produced in the gut that help regulate appetite, digestion and blood sugar.

It’s a similar approach to that used by Eli Lilly’s blockbuster drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound. But ribupatide has been designed to bind more tightly to its targets and stay active in the body longer, potentially extending its effects throughout the week.

Everyone in the study — including those given placebo shots — also followed a lifestyle program that included dietary counseling and recommendations to get at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise each week.

After 48 weeks, those taking the lowest dose of ribupatide had lost an average of 10.7% of their starting body weight. Those on the 4-milligram dose shed 16.4%, while participants taking the highest dose lost a whopping 17.7%.

The placebo group lost just 1.4%.

The numbers are in the same ballpark as — and potentially higher than — those seen with Wegovy. In a separate clinical trial, people taking a 2.4 mg dose of the popular GLP-1 shot lost an average of 14.9% of their body weight over a longer period of 68 weeks.

And ribupatide’s results could have been even more impressive. Weight loss hadn’t started to level off among participants taking the two highest doses by the end of the 11-month study, suggesting they could have lost even more with longer treatment.

And the benefits extended beyond the scale.

Although none of the participants had diabetes, researchers found that those taking ribupatide had reductions in blood sugar. They also saw improvements in blood pressure and cholesterol.

Their waistlines shrank, too — an important measurement because abdominal fat is linked to an increased risk of heart disease and other health problems.

The participants taking ribupatide saw their waist measurements drop by between 9 and 14 centimeters, compared with just 2.5 centimeters among those on the placebo.

The drug wasn’t without some familiar side effects, though. Like other GLP-1s, ribupatide most commonly caused digestive problems, including nausea, vomiting and diarrhea. The researchers said the symptoms were generally mild to moderate and occurred most often as participants increased their doses.

Study authors said their results are promising and come amid a need for more pharmacological treatment options as obesity continues to plague millions of people.

The problem is particularly acute in the US, where roughly four in 10 adults have obesity and an even larger share are overweight. Among children and teenagers ages 2 to 19, just over 21% have obesity.

It’s no wonder Americans’ appetite for weight-loss injections shows little sign of slowing. A September Gallup survey found that 11% of US adults were currently taking a GLP-1 medication for weight loss, up from just 3% in 2024.

Overall, 15% said they had taken one of the blockbuster drugs at some point in their lives — a jump of nine percentage points in just two years.

news.originalContent:

Nvidia fell Monday for the third straight day as investors panicked over the fallout from CEO Jensen Huang’s dramatic ouster – even as President Trump reportedly prepared to designate the chipmaker a “national champion.”

The chipmaker is slated to be among more than two dozen companies labeled AI “national champions” by the Trump administration sometime within the next week, which gives them special export approvals in an attempt to boost overseas business, according to the Wall Street Journal.

Nvidia’s stock was last trading down 1.2% at $160.96 a share after shedding hundreds of billions of dollars in market value last week. It has slipped below the $4 trillion mark, making Apple the world’s most valuable company with a $5.2 trillion market cap.

Huang resigned on Thursday as CEO, president and a member of the chipmaker’s board after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. News reports soon surfaced that he had at least two other affairs with executives at his company.

Many, however, have been calling for Huang to return to the legendary chipmaker he founded 33 years ago and grew into an industry giant – arguing the company won’t maintain its dealmaking prowess without him.

Billionaire Elon Musk is backing an online petition that has garnered more than 170,000 signatures calling for him to be brought back, despite the national security concerns around his affair with Alice Huang, a suspected Communist spy of no relation.

Huang has already agreed to testify before three House committees on China, foreign affairs and intelligence before the Thanksgiving break, and Democratic leaders – now holding powerful majorities – are also expected to haul the disgraced CEO before Congress.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday urged Nvidia to pursue a “dramatic shakeup” among leadership, saying the board should look “outside the company” for its next CEO.

The Commerce Department on Monday announced that it is cracking down on a trade loophole that allowed Chinese firms to access American AI chips and computing power.

Bessent had blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s team for the Chinese spy mess. He said the Treasury, State Department, Defense Department and US Trade Representative had been pushing for the government to blacklist Megaspeed – where Alice Huang worked – “for months.”

In a letter on Sunday, Sen. Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee, also blamed Lutnick and urged the Commerce secretary to reinforce export controls and stop the sale of AI chips to China.

The national champion program is a sign that Trump is still pushing ahead with efforts to boost AI companies and data-center construction, hopeful the industry will lead to blowout American profits.

Companies with the “national champion” designation can receive expedited export approvals, government support for work overseas and federal financing, according to the Commerce Department’s website. The program was announced a year ago, but specific champions have not been named.

Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic are expected to be included in the new program, which is an effort to help American companies succeed over Chinese rivals in foreign business deals, sources told the Wall Street Journal.

Trump reportedly called Huang last week, before the Nvidia CEO stepped down, and urged him to keep fighting for his job, according to the New York Times.

The president has also publicly defended Huang. During an interview last Thursday, Trump told Stephen A. Smith that Huang is “going through hell” and “feels most badly [about] his wife and family.” Trump also told reporters that Huang is an “honorable guy” and said “he probably has an excuse for it.”

Trump’s stake in Nvidia was between $13 million and $62 million as of the end of August, according to a Washington Post review of his financial disclosures.

It’s no secret that lead deckhand Matt Fitzpatrick-Buck has very little confidence in Alex Wright as his bosun on Below Deck Season 13. Early in the charter season, Fitzpatrick-Buck expressed his concerns to Captain Kerry Titheradge, who assured Fitzpatrick-Buck that he was aware of Wright’s shortcomings.

In this exclusive clip from tonight’s all-new episode, Fitzpatrick-Buck is still frustrated with Wright and his organizational skills. The clip begins at 7:45 AM with Fitzpatrick-Buck standing in the lazarette staring at the equipment and water toys that were left out overnight. “This place is not good at all,” says Fitzpatrick-Buck to himself as he assesses the mess. He swears to himself and sits down dejectedly on a cooler. “Sick and tired of doing everything,” mumbles Fitzpatrick-Buck. “Fucking Alex.”

In his confessional, Fitzpatrick-Buck continues to complain. “I’m mad because it’s a fucking buildup over the last two, three weeks,” explains Fitzpatrick-Buck. “Waking up this morning with the boat a fucking mess…I’m sick and tired of cleaning up. I’m fucking over it. Enough is enough.”

Next, Fitzpatrick-Buck goes to the wheelhouse to speak with Titheradge once again about his displeasure with Wright. “Fuck, I’m getting frustrated,” says Fitzpatrick-Buck to Titheradge. “I respect Alex as a person, but I keep on picking up his slack, and it’s pissing me off.”

Titheradge encourages Fitzpatrick-Buck to share his grievances. “Last night, he didn’t give James the job list, and there’s shit tons of stuff to do,” begins Fitzpatrick-Buck. “The last two days on deck, he’s late.” Then, Fitzpatrick-Buck’s complaints get personal. “He just rolls out of bed, doesn’t brush his teeth. He spends the first thirty minutes doing nothing.”

Titheradge listens intently to Fitzpatrick-Buck’s grievances. “I just don’t respect him as a bosun,” finishes Fitzpatrick-Buck. Clearly disappointed by Fitzpatrick-Buck’s observations, Titheradge can only rub his brow in frustration.

Will Titheradge demote Wright and promote Fitzpatrick-Buck? Will Wright get the chance to plead his case? Tune in to Bravo tonight at 8 PM ET for an all-new episode of Below Deck to find out!

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A sick hospital security guard who was caught having sex with an elderly woman’s corpse in a morgue freezer is now facing up to 15 years in prison.

An Arizona jury last week found Randall Bird, 49, guilty of having sex with a dead person — three years after he was discovered by colleagues in the freezer with his belt off and fly down next to the partially naked body of a 79-year-old woman.

The victim, who had died of natural causes, was lying face down on top of a gurney with her body bag unzipped, with Bird’s duty belt on top of her, in the morgue at Banner University Medical Center in Phoenix, according to charging documents obtained by AZ Family after his arrest in November 2023.

The necrophile’s uniform appeared “messy,” and he was “sweating profusely” and “acting very nervous,” co-workers told police.

“They stated that [Bird] had removed his duty belt, which they observed on top of a gurney where a bagged deceased body was placed. [Bird’s] zipper on his uniform pants was wide open, and the rest of his uniform looked all messy,” police wrote in the documents.

“The victim’s hospital gown had been rolled up above her belly button area, exposing her naked body from the waist down,” investigators added, according to The Smoking Gun.

The twisted body desecration was discovered when Bird’s colleagues, who were other security guards, arrived at work around 5:30 a.m. and the main entrance to the morgue unlocked, which was unusual. They then saw the freezer cracked open and inside spotted Bird, who frantically tried to cover the woman’s body.

He told them he had suffered a medical episode, causing him to grab the victim’s body as he fainted and fell to the floor, the documents said.

He insisted the woman’s body bag tore and its zipper broke as a result — but the workers didn’t buy it and reported him to their supervisors. He told police the same story when they interviewed him days later.

Security guards at the hospital are tasked only with transporting dead bodies to the morgue and placing them inside a freezer and are not supposed to open the body bags, officials said.

Investigators collected evidence from the victim and Bird and confirmed his DNA was found on the victim. Post-mortem rib fractures were also found on the victim’s body.

Bird was convicted Thursday by a jury in Arizona Superior Court on four counts of sexual conduct with a dead person, court records show.

He is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. 18, where he is facing between 12 and 45 months for each charge for a maximum of 15 years.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

British women convicted of illegally terminating their pregnancies under a Victorian-era law will be automatically pardoned Monday, the government said.

The action follows Parliament’s passage last year of a landmark vote to decriminalize abortion by repealing a section from the 1861 Offences Against the Person Act.

Women who have received a caution from police will also be pardoned and women arrested or investigated for ending their own pregnancy will have those details removed from their criminal records. They will not have to apply for pardons and some will be issued posthumously.

“For too long, women have faced the devastating consequences of outdated abortion laws,” said Heidi Stewart, chief executive of the British Pregnancy Advisory Service. “While no pardon can undo the distress and trauma these women have experienced, this historic change in the law recognizes the profound harm caused by their criminalization and represents a meaningful step towards justice.”

The government did not provide the number of women affected. But Tonia Antoniazzi, the Labour member of Parliament who introduced the decriminalization amendment, said police had investigated more than 100 women suspected of illegal abortions in the five years preceding last year’s vote. That included some who suffered natural miscarriages and stillbirths.

Antoniazzi described how women suspected of illegally aborting a fetus were once “dragged from hospital beds to police cells” and interrogated when they should have been cared for.

“This trauma cannot be erased, but I hope that this offers some alleviation of the pain these women have endured, enabling them to participate fully in society again, living their lives to the full, working the jobs they’ve always wanted to,” she said.

Under current law, doctors can legally carry out abortions in England, Scotland and Wales up to 24 weeks, and beyond that under special circumstances, such as when the life of the mother is in danger. Abortion in Northern Ireland was decriminalized in 2019.

Under the Crime and Policing Act that took effect this spring, women who terminate a pregnancy at any stage will not face criminal charges.

The measure was opposed by anti-abortion groups that argued it would open the door to abortion on demand at any stage of pregnancy.

The law was changed after high-profile prosecutions, including the jailing of a mother of three that caused an outcry from abortion rights supporters.

Carla Foster was sentenced to more than two years in prison in 2023 for medically inducing an abortion about eight months into her pregnancy. An appeals court freed her a month later, saying the case called for “compassion, not punishment.”

Another woman, Nicola Packer, was acquitted on a charge of unlawfully self-administering poison or a noxious thing with intent to procure a miscarriage. Packer, who took abortion medicine when she was about 26 weeks pregnant, testified that she did not know she had been pregnant more than 10 weeks.

WASHINGTON — The new youngest member of Congress wants you to know one thing about Gen Z.

“Sometimes we hear, ‘Oh, this younger generation, they’re afraid to work.’ That is not true,” insisted Michael Alfonso, a former brick-layer and the 26-year-old Republican congressman-elect from Wisconsin, to The Post.

“The younger generation is ready to work,” said Alfonso, the son-in-law of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Fox News personality Rachel Campos-Duffy.

“They just want to be paid well, and they want an economy that will actually deliver them results for their hard work.”

Alfonso, who is married to the Duffys’ oldest daughter Evita, made history earlier this month by winning Wisconsin’s 7th Congressional District seat. He will become the youngest member of Congress when he takes office in January, besting 29-year-old Rep. Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.).

The 26-year-old ran on an “America First” platform with support from President Trump while overcoming complaints about alleged inexperience and nepotism.

The seat he scored was once held by his father-in-law.

Alfonso said he is motivated to make policy changes in Washington to give young people more opportunities, such as by trying to open up home-buying for them, touting the value of trade schools and two-year tech programs and by tackling affordability issues in general.

The congressman-elect, who mixed concrete and laid brick to pay his way through the University of Wisconsin-Madison, then produced former FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino’s podcast, said Gen Zers are the victims of “dereliction of duty” by their elders.

“We lie to this younger generation,” he said, referring to, for example, the belief that a four-year college degree is the sure route to success.

The younger generation also has to deal with the difficulty of becoming a homeowner.

Alfonso pegged the age of the typical first-time homebuyer at 41, similar to the National Association of Realtors’ estimate of 40.

“It’s up there,” he said. “I mean, it’s ridiculous.”

Alfonso won his seat by 12.8 percentage points Nov. 3, following in the footsteps of Duffy, who repped the rural district between 2011 and 2019.

He noted that unfortunately, his party will spend the 120th Congress in the minority in both the House and Senate.

“We got our teeth kicked in,” Alfonso said.

To try to begin leading the House GOP out of the wilderness, Alfonso has thrown his support behind Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) as the chamber’s next minority leader, the young pol said.

“He’s not necessarily a new face [in the House], but a new face in leadership to maybe kick us in the right direction,” the fresh-faced legislator explained. “We’ve always been the party of meritocracy. Jim Jordan is getting his shot here.

“Focusing here at home should be really our top concern, if not only concern,” Alfonso added when asked if his party had neglected kitchen-table issues over the past two years.

He recalled what his famous father-in-law told him when he revealed he was running for his old seat.

“‘Oh boy, it’s a lot of work. I hope you’re ready for it,’ ” Alfonso said Duffy told him.

Alfonso said he went through four pairs of shoes campaigning.

“If at 26 I can’t be the hardest-working member of Congress, I shouldn’t be here anyways,” he quipped to The Post.

He noted that unfortunately, his party will spend the 120th Congress in the minority in both the House and Senate.

“We got our teeth kicked in,” Alfonso said.

To try to begin leading the House GOP out of the wilderness, Alfonso has thrown his support behind Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) as the chamber’s next minority leader, the young pol said.

“He’s not necessarily a new face [in the House], but a new face in leadership to maybe kick us in the right direction,” the fresh-faced legislator explained. “We’ve always been the party of meritocracy. Jim Jordan is getting his shot here.

“Focusing here at home should be really our top concern, if not only concern,” Alfonso added when asked if his party had neglected kitchen-table issues over the past two years.

He recalled what his famous father-in-law told him when he revealed he was running for his old seat.

“‘Oh boy, it’s a lot of work. I hope you’re ready for it,’ ” Alfonso said Duffy told him.

Alfonso said he went through four pairs of shoes campaigning.

“If at 26 I can’t be the hardest-working member of Congress, I shouldn’t be here anyways,” he quipped to The Post.

news.originalContent:
Eight men killed in shooting near Pietermaritzburg while six men and three women shot dead near Pretoria.

At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, police said.

Eight men were found dead late on Sunday in a “bullet-riddled” vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside the city of Pietermaritzburg, police said.

Hours later, nine people were found dead in Jeffsville, an informal settlement near South Africa’s capital, Pretoria, police said. The bodies of six men and three women were discovered inside a shack with gunshot wounds.

National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola said on Monday that investigators had not established motives for the crimes that took place 530 kilometres (330 miles) apart.

“The ongoing mass shootings which we encounter are unacceptable. Definitely, we have to find these criminals. We cannot allow them to terrorise communities or determine how people live their lives,” Masemola said.

South Africa has struggled for years with high rates of violent crime, but has had a recent surge in mass shootings with high death tolls.

Reporting from Pretoria, Al Jazeera’s Clement Manyathela said the community was “gripped by fear” as it waits for answers about the shooting.

He said the victims were found in a four-room shack, where the killings happened just before midnight. A young child who went into the shack looking for a relative made the discovery, he said.

Pathologists, investigators and officers were working to establish what happened.

Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni said one of those killed was a “person of interest” in a shooting last year in the nearby informal settlement of Saulsville, in which 12 people were killed and 13 wounded, the Associated Press news agency reported.

“We cannot rule out that they may be linked, and may possibly have been a retaliation attack,” Mthombeni said.

In the Pietermaritzburg shooting, police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said some families had come forward to help identify victims.

“It’s still too early to tell what the motive could have been and who could be behind the shooting because we are yet to identify the victims,” said Netshiunda.

news.originalContent:
Ukraine’s military has been relying on the internet service since December 2024 to intercept Russian drones.

Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that limits on SpaceX’s Starshield military-grade internet service are disrupting Ukrainian drone operations and hindering the country’s war effort against Russia.

Over the weekend, two people were killed in a Russian jet-powered drone attack on what Ukrainian officials called “critical infrastructure” in the northern Koriukivka region. An energy facility was also hit in Odesa overnight on Sunday, leaving 41,000 households without electricity.

Zelenskyy linked the success of these Russian strikes to limits that he said had been placed on Ukraine’s use of Starshield. The country’s military has been relying on the service since December 2024 to intercept Russian drones.

Starshield is a sister service to Starlink, a network of 11,000 satellites launched into low Earth orbit by SpaceX  to provide high-speed internet connectivity, even in remote areas.

In a statement on X on Sunday, Zelenskyy said that Russia was targeting energy substations with Shahed drones, which both sides often use to attack each other.

He added that “many of these strikes are getting through because restrictions on the operating speed of Starshield terminals along the front line and in the temporarily occupied territories are still there”.

“We are counting on these restrictions being lifted. The protection of lives and Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ahead of winter directly depends on this,” he added.

Zelenskyy also accused Starlink’s sister service of throttling internet speeds and hampering military operations on Saturday. He said that the internet restrictions had been in place for five days.

This is not the first time Ukrainian officials have complained about limits on Starshield hampering Kyiv’s defence efforts.

Last month, Ukrainian defence officials said they had lost access to important satellite-based communications and that the disruptions had affected military missions. This came in the wake of heavy Russian missile and drone strikes, for which Ukraine said it had received no prior warning.

According to a November 2 report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), Starshield is critical to Ukraine since it helps in encrypting satellite communications, which are needed to guide drones in order to carry out interceptions.

“In addition to using Starshield service for strikes within Ukrainian territory occupied by Russian forces, Ukraine uses Starshield-equipped drones to intercept and defend against Russian drones, such as new jet-powered drones taking aim at Ukrainian critical infrastructure and civilian targets,” the CSIS report noted.

Without access to Starshield internet, these Ukrainian drones are unable to work as effectively.

“Our interceptor drones lose connection with their operators at a speed of 161 kilometres per hour (100 miles per hour) and simply cannot catch up with Russian jet-powered ‘shaheds’,” Zelenskyy said on X on Sunday.

After last month’s disruptions, Zelenskyy said on X that “intelligence on Russian ballistic missile launches helps save lives, and this is one of the most critical issues”.

“This is precisely what helps prevent people from being killed – when there is an early warning about ballistic missiles,” he added.

Last month, Serhiy Beskrestnov, a defence adviser to Zelenskyy, had posted on Telegram that SpaceX had also “implemented a speed limit” on Starlink terminals, capping internet speeds at 100mph (161km/h).

That meant any drones or missiles flying at more than 100mph lost their guidance connection.

“Our armed forces did not receive a warning about these restrictions, and this led to the failure of a number of missions,” he had said, adding that this was clearly “related to the current political situation”.

Officials have said the restrictions have also reduced capabilities for front-line logistics, reconnaissance and relaying signals.

Jet-powered drones are high-speed uncrewed aerial vehicles equipped with small turbojet engines rather than traditional propellers or piston engines.

In its war on Ukraine, Russia has increasingly deployed jet-powered variants such as the Geran-3, Geran-4, and Geran-5 models.

These drones fly at much higher speeds than traditional propeller-powered drones, making them significantly harder for Ukrainian air defences to intercept.

In August, 38 people were killed in the village of Myla in Ukraine, when a Russian drone attack struck an ammunition depot. Another 12 were killed in attacks across the country in September.

Ukraine’s Air Force spokesman Yurii Ihnat said in September that while the country has an interception rate of more than 90 percent against propeller-powered drones, that success rate falls to only 60 percent against jet-powered models.

Ukraine has, however, retaliated using its own drone systems, and has also struck Russian refineries, hitting 12 in August, along with two gas-processing plants and three oil shipment terminals, according to its defence ministry.

On Sunday, Ukraine’s army said it also shot down 106 of 132 Russian drones launched overnight.

But to counter Russia’s jet-powered drones more efficiently, Zelenskyy said he had told teams of Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Defence, and the presidential office “to work as closely as possible with the American side and SpaceX” and remove restrictions on Starshield.

“It is important to be on the right side of history. It is essential to help Ukraine,” he said on Sunday.

Starlink, owned by US billionaire Elon Musk’s SpaceX, is yet to respond to recent accusations about Starshield from Zelenskyy.

But last month, the company and Musk denied restricting internet speeds.

Responding to a post on X by Ukraine’s former Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who said the speed limits were being lifted and demanded unrestricted internet speed, Musk wrote last month, “Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government.”

“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he said, referring to the US president.

Musk further clarified that Starlink is for “civilian or defensive activities and cannot be used for offensive military action, as doing so would be inappropriate for a commercial company” – an apparent attempt to differentiate it from Starshield.

Zelenskyy said in an interview with the Financial Times last month that US military officials had earlier warned Kyiv that Washington would block intelligence unless attacks on Russian energy infrastructure stop.

The Ukrainian leader added that he did not accept suggestions that the Starshield incident could have been a glitch. “It was not a technical problem; it was the will,” he said.

Tensions between Kyiv and Washington have been building since Donald Trump returned to the presidency last year, including over Washington’s increasing reluctance to militarily support Ukraine and its mounting efforts to forge a deal with Russia.

But Trump has said that it is Musk who controls Starlink’s operations in Ukraine.

When asked about internet restrictions in Ukraine, he told reporters last month that Musk had restored Kyiv’s access, while denying any White House role in the episode.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said last month that decisions about Starlink’s speed and access belong to Musk.

“The bottom line is that that is governed by a private commercial contract as to how ⁠⁠⁠⁠their stuff can be used and what speeds they’ll allow it to be used at,” Rubio had said.

Meanwhile, officials from Ukraine and Russia held peace talks in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, last week. The talks, mediated by the US, only yielded an agreement on a prisoner exchange and failed to make a breakthrough on ending the war, which is nearing the five-year mark.

The US, however, pitched a new pathway for Ukraine to join NATO, an aspiration that Kyiv has long held as a means to guarantee its defence against Russia.

According to Zelenskyy, Trump’s administration has suggested that Ukraine would need to agree to give up all of the Donbas region in the country’s east, which Russian President Vladimir Putin has demanded as one of his conditions for ending the war.

On Saturday, Zelenskyy told reporters that the prospect of Ukraine joining NATO in exchange for ceding territory had not been raised by members of the alliance before and reiterated that Kyiv would not give up any of its territories.

But Zelenskyy said if Ukraine received a peace deal which included security guarantees, the right to maintain a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army, and funds to rebuild the country, then he would hold a national referendum on the question of ceding territory in exchange for NATO membership.

The Kremlin has not yet responded to the latest US proposal. But it has maintained a strict position that Ukraine’s NATO membership is a red line for Moscow and a direct threat to Russia’s national security. In fact, Putin has also cited the issue of Ukraine’s NATO aspirations as one reason why Russia launched its war in 2022.

Moscow has, however, insisted that Ukraine should cede sovereignty over the Donbas region, in addition to parts of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson provinces that Russia already occupies.

news.originalContent:
The Germany coach believes anyone who replaces the FIFA president should care deeply about the future of football.

Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has called for an end to Gianni Infantino’s time as FIFA president, saying he “did not think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter”.

Klopp believes the next candidate for the job of leading football’s global governing body should have the game’s interests at heart.

“I’ve been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense,” Klopp said on Sunday in Berlin ahead of his team’s Nations League clash with the Netherlands.

“I didn’t think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that.”

President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations. He later faced charges before being cleared in two trials, but was banned from football by FIFA’s ethics committee.

Klopp added: “Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job.”

Swiss-born Infantino, who succeeded Blatter as FIFA president in 2016, has been criticised for a series of decisions and proposals, including his plan to sell off part of the commercial rights of the World Cup. He was also lambasted for last year’s creation of the FIFA Peace Prize, and for giving the inaugural award to United States President Donald Trump.

“There are people who truly care about the future of football — people who aren’t driven by financial interests,” said Klopp. “If someone like that were to step up — if someone like that were to become president — I think that would be a significant improvement.”

“There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it,” he added.

The next election for FIFA president takes place in March 2027. Only former Swiss footballer Ramon Vega and Japan’s Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to run against Infantino.

news.originalContent:
Romelu Lukaku, Belgium’s all-time leading goalscorer, has announced his retirement from international football after 16 years, saying he was “at peace” with his decision.

“These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team. It was a nice ride and I enjoyed every single moment,” Belgium’s record goalscorer said on Instagram on Monday.

With 94 goals in 135 games, Lukaku is the fifth-highest scorer in men’s international football history and featured in four World Cups for the Red Devils, helping them reach the quarterfinals of this year’s tournament before losing to eventual winners Spain.

The 33-year-old, who now plays for Turkish club Fenerbahce, made his debut in 2010 as a teenager and was an unused substitute in Sunday’s 4-1 Nations League win over Italy.

“To the Belgium fans, thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

“I will never forget those moments. I’m at peace with my decision to stop here,” Lukaku said.

The former Chelsea, Manchester United and Inter Milan forward was part of Belgium’s so-called “golden generation”.

Lukaku, alongside Kevin De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, finished third at the 2018 World Cup, a best-ever finish for Belgium in the tournament, but they failed to lift a trophy during the period.

“I played with amazing teammates that I will always be grateful for,” Lukaku said.

“I want to thank them all. I want to thank all the coaches as well for pushing and trusting me to help the team,” he added.

The national team paid homage to Lukaku shortly after his announcement.

“More than a goalscorer, you have been a leader, a strong personality and an inspiration to generations of Belgian football fans,” said a post on Instagram by the Red Devils. “You have written an incredible chapter in the history of the Red Devils.”

A host of fellow Belgian players also paid tribute to Lukaku.

“Legend, my brother,” midfielder Axel Witsel posted on Instagram.

“Thank you for everything my bro,” Courtois said.

“So many amazing memories,” the Real Madrid goalkeeper added.

Lukaku’s last appearance for his country came in October’s 4-1 loss to France.

“Beyond his exceptional performances on the pitch, he has been a true leader, with a strong personality and an essential role in the dressing room,” Lukaku’s former teammate and now Belgium’s technical director, Simon Mignolet, said in a statement from the Belgian football association.

“We respect his decision and are deeply grateful to him for everything he has brought to our national team,” the former Liverpool goalkeeper added.

Belgium’s first game without Lukaku will be a Nations League last-eight fixture in March.

“We must now turn our attention to the future and prepare for the Nations League quarterfinals … with the ambition of continuing to make progress as a team,” Mignolet said.

A rape conviction for the British comedian and actor leads to a reckoning for the media that kept him in the spotlight.

The conviction of comedian and actor Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault is a moment of reckoning for Britain’s entertainment industry. Some of the country’s most influential media institutions gave him the platforms, credibility and audiences that made him such a prominent public figure, and continued to do so as more and more allegations of sexual misconduct and predatory behaviour surfaced.

Dorothy Byrne – Former head of news and current affairs, Channel 4
Caroline Frost – Entertainment journalist
Dalia Gebrial – Lecturer, King’s College London and author of Decolonising the University

Meenakshi Ravi reports on how the outlet went toe-to-toe with the Kremlin.

Elettra Scrivo reports on one of the world’s most entrenched gambling industries, the advertising that props it up and the lobby that protects it.

news.originalContent:
A nine-month-old baby has died from hypothermia inside his family’s displacement tent in Gaza, as winter returns.

Khan Younis, Gaza Strip – For Susan Arqiq, the hardest part of the day comes at night, when the noise around her fades and she is left alone with the absence of her nine-month-old son, Kinan. She is still struggling to understand how the cold took his life.

Susan, 26, had put him to sleep beside her on Wednesday night, as she had done countless times before, at their camp in Khan Younis. When she woke in the early hours of the morning to change his diaper, she found Kinan’s face blue, his hands stiff and his body cold.

Her arms, which had held him through countless nights, are now empty.

“My son was pressed against the tent’s tarpaulin. The bedding was still damp,” she told Al Jazeera.

“I switched on my phone’s flashlight and found that his face was completely blue, his hands were stiff, and his body was like ice. My heart nearly stopped from fear. I immediately woke my husband. I was screaming, ‘Kinan, Kinan!’ I could not understand what was wrong with him.”

Her husband did not speak. He picked up the baby and, accompanied by men from the camp, rushed him to hospital.

Women from neighbouring tents, woken by the cries, gathered around Susan. They tried to reassure her that her baby would be all right, but the news from the hospital confirmed her fears.

Kinan died on Thursday, November 12, after a severe drop in his body temperature, according to medical sources. His death was the first cold-related fatality recorded in Gaza during the current winter season.

Susan and her husband, Ahmed Arqiq, 33, have been in shock since the tragic death of their son. Ahmed says Kinan had no known health problems before that night.

“At the emergency department, they told me, ‘May God compensate you. The child has died, and the cause is the severe drop in temperature,’” Ahmed says. “I was shocked… My heart is broken, and even now I cannot believe it.”

Israel’s war on Gaza, which began in October 2023, has seen at least 73,600 Palestinians killed and large parts of the occupied Palestinian territory reduced to rubble. Due to the destruction of their homes or Israeli military occupation, around 1.4 million people are living in tents or makeshift displacement camps.

Israel’s siege on Gaza has prevented mobile homes, tarpaulins, and other essential materials from entering the territory.

The Arqiq family are one of many living in a worn-out displacement tent in the al-Mawasi camp near Khan Younis in southern Gaza as winter approaches. The shelter offers little protection from the cold or the rain, which flooded camps across Gaza during a storm last week.

Ahmed has been unable to find work since the war, and they struggle to afford even the basic necessities of life.

“I have struggled to obtain adequate shelter, blankets, clothing and food for my children. My life is all about suffering,” he said. “Look at my tent. We live in poor conditions. During the last winter storm, we were flooded with water.”

Ahmed said the family had not received a proper tent or tarpaulin to protect them from the winter weather before Kinan’s death. After Kinan died, they received the waterproof sheet, but it was too late to protect him.

Kinan was the youngest of three children, and his brothers, Rami, three, and Ali, two, were deeply attached to him. They continue to ask about their younger brother, unable to understand why he is no longer with them.

“They always ask where he has gone. Whenever they see his belongings, they try to look for him. It is unbelievable,” Ahmed said.

Kinan’s death has renewed fears among displaced families in Gaza as winter sets in. Last week, heavy rain and flooding battered displacement camps across Gaza, damaging tents and leaving families exposed to cold and wet conditions. At least four children died in the floods.

Babies are particularly vulnerable to hypothermia as their bodies are less able to regulate temperature, especially when exposed to cold for prolonged periods.

At least 11 people are believed to have died due to the cold in Gaza last winter.

Hadeel al-Midana, 27, lives in a displacement tent west of Gaza City with her three children: Hamza and his two older brothers, Mahmoud, seven, and Nour al-Din, five. Her husband, Ibrahim, has been out of work since the war.

She said Kinan’s death has deepened fears she carries each night when she tries to keep her own youngest son, one-month-old Hamza, warm.

“I am always on edge. I cannot leave him,” she told Al Jazeera.

The family struggles to keep the children warm with limited clothing and blankets.

“I swear, he doesn’t have a blanket of his own. I wrap him in the blankets that I use myself,” Hadeel says, referring to Hamza.

The family has received second-hand clothes from neighbours. They were also provided with four blankets at the camp, but Hadeel said the cold inside their tent remains difficult to endure.

“Even the adults cannot bear it. How much worse is it for the little children?” she asked.

She wakes up several times during the night to check on Hamza. Two nights ago, she found his hands and feet were as cold as ice. Terrified, she covered him with a thicker blanket.

She says she needs more blankets for her baby and a small bed to lift him off the ground.

“I need blankets for him, and perhaps a bed that would raise him a little above the ground. I am afraid of the insects, too,” she said.

“The tent is not fit for a child’s life, or even an adult’s life. We live in constant fear, and there is nothing we can do to face it. I hope we get through this winter safely.”

news.originalContent:
Photo by Julie JAMMOT / AFP via Getty Images

Anthropic’s latest artificial intelligence model is spitting out elaborate digital creations in hours as the company releases more products that automate your work.

Claude Fable 5.2, which Anthropic released Nov. 9, can complete 41.25 percent of real freelance projects, according to the Remote Labor Index (RLI). Chinese-founded startup Butterfly Effect’s Manus agent was the top performer when the RLI debuted in Oct. 2025, successfully accomplishing 2.5 percent of freelance tasks.

“Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision,” the company said in its announcement. Fable is the publicly available version of the Mythos 5.2 model, which is limited to “vetted” researchers.

Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5 and rival OpenAI’s GPT 6 Astra can each perform roughly 21 percent of freelance tasks in the test, according to RLI.

The company also announced three new apps on Nov. 10: Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards and Claude Data. These products allow Claude users to create spreadsheets, organize a digital whiteboard and visualize data. (RELATED: Teachers Unions, Anthropic Strike Deal To Protect Student Data)

Anthropic did not immediately respond to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment.

An X user identified as “Chris,” the founder of AI automation company Atonomi, showed that he used Fable 5.2 to design detailed 3D home interiors based on 2D layouts.

“[C]laude [F]able 5.2 is f*cking insane … it can turn 2d blueprints into full 3d walkthroughs that you can tour,” he wrote in a Nov. 10 X post accompanied by a video.

claude fable 5.2 is f*cking insane it can turn 2d blueprints into full 3d walkthroughs that you can tour these go for $5k to $10k per plan and there’s a huge market for them: > home builders selling homes off plan > architects presenting a design to a client > interior designers presenting a renovation > developers selling apartments off plan > kitchen and bath remodelers selling upgrades here’s how to start this business: > pick one niche and find businesses with plans on their site > give fable the blueprint and their photos > it renders a few rooms with gpt image 2.5 or a short clip with seedance as the sample > send them the sample of their own plan before you pitch > once they pay, fable builds the full walkthrough to scale > charge per plan to do the rest of their catalog give this prompt to fable to get started: <role> you find businesses that sell spaces from drawings and turn their 2d floor plans into photoreal homes you can walk through in a browser. you handle the outreach and the build. every room is judged against the client’s own photos, and nothing ships until it holds up next to them. </role> <brief> - niche: [home builders / architects / interior designers / developers / remodelers] - area: [state or city] - offer: a free sample of their own plan, then the full walkthrough per plan - my details: [name, email, calendar link] - news.originalContent:
(Photo by ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images)

Marco Rubio reached back more than 2,000 years to a Roman general to warn the International Criminal Court (ICC) that its rulings carry no force over Americans.

The secretary of state delivered the message during a keynote to the Federalist Society’s National Lawyers Convention in Washington Friday, according to a State Department transcript.

The same answer the Roman commander Pompey once gave to those citing their city’s charters against his legions would greet any move to enforce the court’s decrees on U.S. citizens, Rubio stated. “Stop quoting laws to men with swords,” he said. The line drew laughter, and he joked that the words were not politically correct.

FULL REMARKS: Secretary of State Marco Rubio Delivers Keynote Address, Answers Questions at Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention https://t.co/I9Zbat5ZVY

Rubio accused the court and its global-bureaucracy allies of making themselves “judge and jury and executioner of the international order” while answering to no one, according to the transcript. The tribunal now claims the power to investigate, prosecute and jail Americans under rules the country never approved, he stated. (RELATED: Trump Admin Announces Sanctions Against International Criminal Court Chief)

The secretary cast international law itself as a weapon of a global elite, arguing that critics had wielded it against nearly every major foreign policy decision of the Trump administration, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported. He pointed to the U.S. military’s strikes on cartel boats in the Caribbean and the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro as moves that drew such objections, and he turned the same scorn on the United Nations.

The address was Rubio’s first major speech at home since Republicans absorbed heavy losses in this month’s midterm elections, and the crowd met him with a standing ovation, AFP reported. His choice of a prominent legal audience fed new speculation about a 2028 presidential bid, according to the Hill.

The appearance followed the sweeping sanctions the administration placed on the court in October as part of a campaign it says will dismantle the tribunal, the Associated Press (AP) reported. Washington signed the treaty that created the ICC yet never ratified it, which leaves the United States outside the court alongside Israel, Russia and China, AFP reported.

Enforcement is where the court runs thin, since it fields no police force and leans on member nations to arrest anyone it indicts, AP reported. The United States is not one of them.

Rubio tied the fight to national identity in closing. “To submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats would be to betray who we are, to betray ourselves,” he stated in the remarks.

news.originalContent:
At least 11 employees at two of America’s most powerful intelligence and cyber warfare agencies have died by suicide over the past year, prompting scrutiny from Congress and the White House.

The deaths occurred among military personnel, civilian employees and contractors working for the National Security Agency (NSA) and U.S. Cyber Command, including five suicides within roughly one month that military officials classified as a suicide cluster, according to The Japan Times. The deaths have prompted congressional inquiries and new restrictions on working hours as the agencies grapple with mounting operational demands from overseas conflicts, although officials have not determined that workplace pressures caused the suicides.

The Pentagon referred the Daily Caller News Foundation to Cyber Command who did not respond for comment. The NSA also did not respond to the DCNF’s request for comment. (RELATED: ‘Leadership Doesn’t Know Anything Else’: Why Are Suicide Rates In US Military So High?)

“The pace of operations right now at both NSA and Cyber Command can be overwhelming,” said Harry Coker Jr., a former senior executive at the NSA and Central Intelligence Agency told The Japan Times. “There is a lot of stress that a lot of us overlook because we think cyber is away from the front, and physically that’s accurate but intellectually and emotionally it’s inaccurate.”

Stallings’ family remembered him as as a devoted and discreet officer. He loved riding his motorcycle, reading Green Lantern comics and his chihuahua, Scud. As a kid, he covered his bedroom with glow-in-the-dark stars and stayed up late, reading under the blankets by flashlight. https://t.co/41wtOy924W

From early June to early July, five employees at the NSA and Cyber Command took their lives. These were categorized as cluster suicides, a phenomenon defined as when “suicides or suicide attempts happen closer together in time, location, or both than expected,” per the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The most recent suicide was in September.

This timeline of this cluster coincides with America shifting from a fragile ceasefire agreement with Iran to renewed fighting, according to United States Central Command (CENTCOM).

Even as legislators and military officials made efforts towards addressing the unique mental health challenges faced by these personnel, the suicides continued. Of the ten suicides, nine took place in Fort Meade, Maryland and one in Georgia, according to The Japan Times.

Congressional committees overseeing the military and intelligence agencies requested briefings from both agencies regarding the suicides and workload stress. Tim Kosiba, the NSA’s deputy director, went to the White House to brief officials, per the outlet.

NSA and Cyber Command leaders said that each servicemember had distinctly different motives for ending their lives including personal and financial issues. Technical Sergeant Kevin Stallings referred to a “wall of debt,” his divorce, an earlier suicide in his military unit and the death of his dog, Scud, for his June 11 suicide. Stallings apologized to his military leaders in his suicide note, saying they could not have prevented it.

news.originalContent:
Costa Rica’s Rebeca Grynspan is the current frontrunner, polls suggest, but the US and Russia could veto her bid.

A tense race to replace outgoing United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres is heading into its final few weeks in advance of a deadline that has never been breached, as global powers spar over candidates in an opaque election process.

With eight candidates, secret polls and geopolitical rivalries at play, the choice of the UN’s next chief is still up in the air, even as Guterres must leave office on December 31.

Competing interests from the Americas to the Middle East have complicated the process, raising fears that, for the first time in history, the new year could begin without a leader at the helm of the world’s central diplomatic organisation. The late inclusion of two candidates — Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh and Turkish nominee Feridun Sinirlioglu — has further split the race wide open, with no name so far succeeding in overcoming opposition from all five permanent members of the UN Security Council (UNSC), who hold vetoes.

The protracted contest is part of a “struggle over who will exercise political influence within the UN at a time when multilateralism is under considerable pressure and attack”, Georgina Holmes, senior lecturer in politics and international studies at the Open University, United Kingdom, told Al Jazeera.

“P5 member states are not as politically aligned as they have been in previous eras, arguably even during the Cold War,” said Holmes, referring to the permanent members of the UNSC.

The UN secretary-general has often been compared with a “secular pope” – a figure expected to unite countries and spearhead global diplomacy.

But the position is more than that of a figurehead. The secretary-general is also the UN’s top administrative official, responsible for tapping senior officials and supervising the UN Secretariat’s tens of thousands of staff.

“The secretary-general must be a skilled politician to navigate the geopolitics; a skilled diplomat and mediator to help settle disputes; a charismatic person in the public eye; and a solid and skilled administrator,” Jan Klabbers, professor of international law at the University of Cambridge, told Al Jazeera. “It has been called ‘the most difficult job in the world’ for a reason.”

This year’s race comes as the UN, under Guterres, is under heavy strain, having been sidelined from conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. It has faced blistering criticism from United States President Donald Trump and is suffering a financial crisis that has forced it to let go of thousands of staff.

It also comes as wider geopolitical rivalries extend to the pool of candidates to lead the organisation, who are being scrutinised over their nationalities and policy commitments.

Eight individuals who have been appointed by UN member states are currently in the running to replace Guterres. Most of them are from Latin America or the Caribbean, which is in line with representation according to informal UN protocol. Five of the eight are women, amid a push for the UN to select its first female secretary-general.

A leading contender, according to a series of anonymous straw polls the UNSC carries out to gauge support, is Costa Rican diplomat Rebeca Grynspan.

In the last poll on November 5, which does not show which UNSC members voted which way, Grynspan received 12 “encourage” votes and three “discourage” votes, according to PassBlue, a nonprofit that reports on UN affairs.

Grynspan, who heads the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), has been described as a “continuity candidate”, but there are concerns as to whether she would bring enough reform to an organisation facing huge political and financial pressures.

Richard Gowan, programme director of global issues and institutions at the International Crisis Group, told Al Jazeera that Grynspan had “solidified her position as the frontrunner”, but still appears to face opposition from the US and Russia, which could veto her bid.

While she has avoided directly confronting any veto-wielding nation, some of her reports as UNCTAD head have voiced concerns over Israel’s actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, positions at odds with Washington’s more full-throated support for Israel. Grynspan has previously also disagreed with Russian justifications for suspending a deal to allow the transport of grain through the Black Sea.

At the same time, she — like other candidates — is believed to be lobbying with key member states to win their support. In April, she met Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov over her candidature.

“Grynspan’s team argue that they can still nudge Washington and Moscow to accept her, and US officials do seem to be leaving open the possibility of working with her in the end,” said Gowan.

To be elected, a candidate needs at least nine votes in favour in the 15-member UNSC, while avoiding any vetoes from its five permanent members – the US, the UK, France, Russia and China. The 193-member UN General Assembly (UNGA) then ultimately has to sign off.

Ben Donaldson, adviser to the 1 for 8 Billion campaign, a civil society campaign “advocating for a fair, open, inclusive way to select the next secretary-general”, stressed that opposition from P5 members in a straw poll does not necessarily equate to an eventual veto.

“It has been used in the past as a basis to extract a concession from a candidate, very often in the form of a backroom deal to get a P5 national appointed to a key role in the future UN boss’s cabinet,” he told Al Jazeera.

The Argentinian head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Rafael Grossi, is also in the running. He finished second in the latest straw poll, with nine “encourage” and four “discourage” votes. However, his reputation for being closely aligned with Washington is expected to hurt him with some P5 members, especially China and Russia, though he has also had warm words for Beijing and Moscow in recent weeks.

The other candidates from Latin America or the Caribbean are Guyanese diplomat Carolyn Rodrigues Birkett, Antigua and Barbuda diplomat Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Ecuadorian diplomat Ivonne A-Baki.

Rodrigues Birkett, whose description of Israel’s actions in Gaza as “genocide” has drawn scrutiny in the US, received five “discourage” votes in the latest straw poll. Espinosa and A-Baki received 10 and 14 “discourage” votes, respectively, making their candidacies unlikely.

The UAE’s Lana Nusseibeh and Turkiye’s Feridun Sinirlioglu, nominated by their countries in recent weeks, have also shaken up the race but face significant opposition.

Nusseibeh is reportedly favoured by the US and Russia, but her candidacy has received pushback over her country’s alleged arming of paramilitary forces accused of atrocities in Sudan. The United Arab Emirates has denied the allegation. Nusseibeh received six “discourage” votes in the latest straw poll.

“Nusseibeh’s main challenge is to win over China, which has so far seemed sceptical about her candidacy,” said Gowan. “If she can get Beijing’s support, she could break through.”

Sinirlioglu’s candidature, which UNSC member Greece is expected to oppose, received eight “discourage” votes.

Ugandan politician Olara Otunnu, the only remaining African candidate, received nine “discourage” votes.

Far-right former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban, though not an official candidate, has also been floated by the US as an outside choice, The Wall Street Journal has reported.

Several analysts told Al Jazeera that Grynspan appears to be in the best position, though the influence of P5 countries could change the race.

Earlier this month, the US and Russia put their weight behind the UAE’s Nusseibeh, with France and the UK offering “little resistance”, according to diplomats cited by media platform Devex.

China, for its part, has signalled a preference for a Latin American candidate, reports The New York Times, although Beijing has not publicly endorsed anyone.

Ellen Ravndal, associate professor in political science at the University of Stavanger, Norway, told Al Jazeera the drawn-out selection process and struggle to reach consensus reflect an era of “more geopolitical tensions” and a UN that is in “near-constant crisis mode”.

Adam Day, head of the Geneva office of the United Nations University Centre for Policy Research, pointed out that while the leadership contest has been lengthier and more contested than in the previous cycles in which former Secretaries-General Guterres in 2016 and Ban Ki-moon in 2006 were elected, some earlier races stretched into December.

“In the broader scope of secretary-general races, this one is still within the range of what has been normal,” Day told Al Jazeera. “But the longer it takes, the less time the incoming secretary-general has to prepare a transition.”

If no successor to Guterres is selected by the end of the year, the UN Charter does not specify an automatic interim successor. Any gap in the post would therefore require the UNSC and other UN bodies to agree on how to manage organisational leadership and operations.

“There is widespread concern that the United States and possibly other influential states are running down the clock, potentially to increase pressure to settle for a less popular candidate or to leave the UN leaderless and weakened for a period,” said Donaldson.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

“Kindergarten Cop” villain Richard Tyson has spoken out after the death of former child co-star Christian Cousins.

“I was saddened to hear of the passing of Christian Cousins, who, alongside his twin brother Joseph, starred with me in ‘Kindergarten Cop,’” Tyson wrote in a heartfelt Facebook tribute Sunday.

“It’s hard to believe that more than 35 years have passed since we made that film together.”

Tyson, who played the ruthless drug dealer Cullen Crisp — the on-screen father of Cousins’ character — in the 1990 action comedy, said Cousins was part of a remarkable cast that helped make “Kindergarten Cop” a movie that “continues to bring joy to audiences around the world.”

“My heartfelt condolences go out to his brother Joseph, his family, friends & all those who knew and loved him,” Tyson wrote.

“Rest in peace, Christian. You will always be part of our Kindergarten Cop family.”

Cousins, 43, was found dead at his home in Irvine, California, after concerned family members were unable to reach him.

Irvine police responded to a welfare check at his home just after noon on Oct. 20, TMZ reported.

Police said there was no indication of suspicious circumstances.

Although an official cause of death has not been released, Cousins’ half-brother, Jonas Roeser, revealed in an Instagram post that the actor had been battling liver disease.

“It’s hard to share that my brother, Christian Cousins, has passed away,” Roeser wrote in October.

“Christian and his twin brother, Joseph ‘Joey’ Cousins, are my brothers through my biological father,” he explained, adding that the twins were raised in California while he grew up in Washington, and that he “didn’t get to know them until I was in college.”

Long before they met, Roeser said, he watched his brothers on the prime-time soap “Knots Landing” and in the 1990 hit comedy “Kindergarten Cop.”

He said he’ll always remember Christian as “a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams.”

“I hope your soul is at rest and that you’ve found peace. You are my brother and you will be missed,” Roeser concluded.

Christian and Joey were born in March 1983 in Orange County, California.

The twins landed their first acting gig on an episode of “Highway to Heaven” before sharing the role of Bobby Gibson Ewing in nearly 60 episodes of “Knots Landing” from 1987 to 1992 — a run that overlapped with their big-screen turn in “Kindergarten Cop.”

Their final role came in the 1995 comedy “Twin Sitters,” according to IMDb.

news.originalContent:
Martine Moise is one of ​33 registered candidates running in Haiti’s first presidential election in a decade.

The widow of Haiti’s slain President Jovenel Moise, whose 2021 ⁠assassination was ⁠a major turning point for the nation, has registered as a candidate for the first presidential election in a decade.

Martine Moise’s name appeared on the website of the Provisional Electoral Council (CEP) as a candidate ⁠on Sunday.

A ⁠first-round vote is set for July next year.

Haiti last held a presidential election in 2016. Successive leaders have repeatedly delayed elections, citing insecurity risks, amid the expanding influence of powerful and heavily armed gangs.

“Haiti will rise again on its own two feet, because politics needs to be done differently,” Moise, who has not publicly commented on the registration, said on X last week.

In the post, she also blamed “the opposition” for bringing the country “to its knees”. “They do not want the country to develop; they do not want the people to live well,” she said.

Martine Moise is one of three ‌women among 33 registered presidential candidates. Among other prominent candidates are Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert, both former presidents, former Prime Minister Claude Joseph and former Foreign Minister Dominique Dupuy.

Several candidates, including Martelly and Privert, have been sanctioned internationally over accusations, which they both deny, of supporting armed gangs.

Martine Moise has been a key witness in the Miami court case prosecuting dozens of suspects involved in the murder of her husband, who led ⁠Haiti from 2017 until his death in July 2021.

He ⁠was shot in his bedroom by Colombian mercenaries impersonating agents of the United States Drug Enforcement Administration. Martine Moise suffered serious gunshot wounds and was flown to a hospital in Florida.

PHOENIX — Quentin Grimes broke out of his early-season shooting slump in a major way during the Lakers’ 131-123 win over the Suns on Sunday at Mortgage Matchup Center.

And he arguably had the biggest sequence of the game to seal the victory.

After the Suns cut what was once a 31-point Lakers lead late in the third quarter to five points with just over a minute left in the game, Jake LaRavia missed a corner 3-pointer that could’ve given the Lakers a larger cushion or given the Suns an opportunity to make it a single-possession game.

Grimes made sure the latter didn’t happen, crashing the offensive glass and grabbing the rebound off LaRavia’s miss to give the Lakers another shot at scoring.

The veteran wing took matters into his own hands when he banked in a pull-up 3 to put the Lakers up 129-121 with 32.2 seconds left to ice the game.

Did Grimes call bank before making the game-sealing 3?

“I called game,” Grimes said before repeating the line twice. “I mean, the bank ain’t open on Sunday. I called game. Trying to get out of here and get back to L.A.”

That line should sound familiar.

Paul Pierce, who was playing for the Wizards at the time, famously responded “I called game!” after banking in the game-winning shot of Game 3 of the Wizards’ Eastern Conference Semifinals playoff series against the Hawks.

While Grimes had fun with his response to whether he intentionally banked in the 3, Sunday was an important step for him to break out of his shooting slump.

The sixth-year guard made a season-high five 3s against the Suns, with his performance on Sunday increasing his 3-point percentage from 24.2% to 33.3%.

The Lakers are confident Grimes, who’s shot just over 36% on 3s for his career, will continue to find his groove with his perimeter shot.

“Watching him every day, when he is in the gym, he’s very consistent with his routine,” coach JJ Redick said. “And we tell players this all the time: Whether you’re shooting well or you’re shooting poorly, you should just keep the same routine. Because otherwise, then it becomes, ‘is shooting a superstitious thing?’ I don’t think it is, right? Shooting is based on form and reps and confidence, and the only way to build that confidence is through the reps.

“He’s just handled it really well. He’s been in the gym, he’s got the shots up, he’s done his routine. He’s historically had some really good shooting seasons both from catch-and-shoot and off-the-dribble. We don’t think he’s a 26% [3-point shooter] or whatever he is, I don’t know what he’s been before [Sunday] but somewhere in the 20s. He’s a high 30s guy.”

news.originalContent:

It was just a month ago that Simon Holmstrom, after scoring just once in the season’s first seven games and after a training camp Islanders coach Pete DeBoer described as a “slow start,” was dropped to the fourth line.

That was in some measure a luxury of the team’s depth. Two games later in Toronto, Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie both left injured and the idea of putting someone like Holmstrom that far down in the lineup became, for the moment, impossible. But it also told you the Islanders needed more from a player who’d hovered around the 20-goal mark in each of the last two seasons.

“We actually moved him down in the lineup to try and get his work rate up,” DeBoer said Saturday night after Holmstrom’s first career hat trick put an exclamation mark on the Islanders’ 6-2 win over the Ducks. “Just shift-to-shift work rate. He did that really quickly, and when he does that, his skill takes over.”

Saturday night was an outlier in the sense that Holmstrom had never scored three times in a game before. While Holmstrom was as soft-spoken as ever afterward, he wore a beaming grin that might as well have been lifted from the day prior, when he and the Islanders’ other Swedes, Victor Eklund and Emil Heineman, accompanied the club’s social media team on a trip to Disneyland.

“I thought it’s been a good trip for us,” Holmstrom said. “We had four lines that can score goals and can defend hard, and I thought we did a good job of that today.”

Zoom out and look at the last month, and Saturday looks more like something Holmstrom has been building toward.

In his past 12 games, Holmstrom has 13 points (eight goals, five assists). After those two games on the fourth line, he’s been stapled to Bo Horvat’s wing on the top line. Lately, he’s produced like someone who wants to stay there even as Maccelli, Mathew Barzal and, eventually, Ritchie, come back into the fold.

He’s taking a four-game point streak back home for the Islanders match against Columbus on Tuesday, over which he’s got five points and three assists. The Islanders have been explicit about wanting to integrate Barzal back slowly coming off a serious knee issue, and seem to be doing the same with Maccelli as well, putting him on the fourth line.

Holmstrom’s play — along with the second line’s recent success — is giving them the luxury to do that. “Well, he’s got a great shot. He’s playing with really good players,” DeBoer said. “They’re finding him, but he’s finishing those opportunities. He had a slow start, I thought, to camp and to the season. He’s gotten better every night.”

There was a two-step-forward, one-step-back element to the Islanders’ health out West, as both Jean-Gabriel Pageau and Logan Stanley went down as they were getting other players back. There was some optimism though, at least initially, that neither of those injuries would be long term. Ritchie is also skating on his own back in New York, and in week four of the initial 4-6 week timeline he was given to return.

In other words, the Islanders can squint and see a healthy team around the corner, a luxury they haven’t had all season.

Already, the Islanders had to make a roster move to activate Barzal, waiving Kyle MacLean, who was sent to AHL Hamilton on Sunday after clearing. He won’t be the last casualty.

The question of what that lineup will look like has been a fun parlor game all season. Holmstrom might be changing the answer.

CINCINNATI  — Joe Burrow passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns, Ja’Marr Chase had 11 catches for 231 yards and the Cincinnati Bengals dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18 on Sunday night to move into sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

Running back Chase Brown had 82 scrimmage yards and scored two touchdowns, both receiving, as the Bengals (7-2) extended their winning streak to five games. It was the first time in four opportunities that a team has played in Europe the week before and beaten an opponent coming off a bye.

Cincinnati’s defense sacked Pittsburgh’s Aaron Rodgers three times as the 42-year-old quarterback had one of the worst games of his 22-year career. Rodgers did not have his first completion until his eighth attempt, a 5-yard throw to tight end Dwayne Washington off play-action with four minutes remaining in the first half.

Burrow completed 35 of 44 and had a 135.7 passer rating. He was lifted for Joe Flacco midway through the fourth quarter. It was the 10th 400-yard game of Burrow’s seven-year NFL career and his third this season. The 409 yards were tied for the sixth most Pittsburgh has allowed to a quarterback.

Pittsburgh (6-3) struggled in all three phases until the fourth quarter. Rodgers was 15 of 29 for 129 yards with fourth-quarter TD passes to DK Metcalf and Pat Freiermuth.

Jaylen Warren, who came in sixth in the league in scrimmage yards, had only 41 yards. He was held to seven carries for 15 yards after rushing for 127 yards in the Steelers’ 30-27 victory over the Bengals in Week 3.

Burrow had a dominant first half for the second straight week as the Bengals roared out to a 24-3 lead. The seventh-year quarterback topped 300 yards in the first half for the second time in his NFL career as he completed 26 of 34 passes for 302 yards with touchdowns to Brown, Drew Sample and Dohnte Meyers.

The Bengals scored on four of their five first-half possessions. The only time they didn’t score was when Evan McPherson was wide right from 43 yards midway through the second quarter, ending his run of 25 straight field goals.

Igor Shesterkin was moved to season-ending injured reserve Sunday, The Post’s Mollie Walker confirmed, a move that will keep the Rangers star goalie out through not just the regular season, but the playoffs as well.

So even if the Rangers reach the postseason, Shesterkin won’t be available.

It also means the team can bump its long-term injured reserve relief to around $10.5 million, which allows them to add to their payroll.

Fortunately for the Blueshirts, their goalie situation has stabilized since Shesterkin was lost to a knee injury.

Thanks to the play of Joonas Korpisalo, who was out for most of the early part of the season with a foot infection, the Rangers have gotten solid performances from both the veteran goalie and rookie Dylan Garand.

“Prior to [Korpisalo’s return], we gave Dylan a very heavy workload, more than we’d like,’’ head coach Mike Sullivan said. “I don’t think that sets any goalie up for success. We have the ability to share the workload so one doesn’t get overburdened.”

In their past six games, a stretch in which they’ve gone 5-1, the Rangers haven’t allowed more than three goals to any opponent, and it’s clear they will use both Garand and Korpisalo evenly moving forward.

The Rangers also traded for goalie Arvid Soderblom from the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for goaltender Spencer Martin. Soderblom, 27, appeared in five games for the Blackhawks this season and will be assigned to AHL Hartford. He’s played in parts of six seasons in Chicago. Martin played in seven games over two seasons with the Rangers.

Pavel Dorofeyev was on the ice briefly for Sunday’s practice but was removed for “precautionary reasons,” according to the team.

Asked if there was any concern Dorofeyev could miss Monday’s game at Madison Square Garden against the Montreal Canadiens, Sullivan said, “Not to my knowledge.”

Dorofeyev has scored four goals in his past nine games after putting up just a pair of goals in his first dozen games as a Ranger.

Sean Durzi, sidelined with an undisclosed injury, last played Oct. 26 but was on the ice with the team during Sunday’s practice in a noncontact jersey.

“He’s getting there,’’ Sullivan said of the defenseman. “He’s making progress.”

He’ll still need to become a full participant before he can return to the lineup.

J.T. Miller was booed throughout Friday’s win over Vancouver in his second trip back after being traded from the Canucks to the Rangers.

“It caught me a little off guard in the beginning,’’ Miller said with a smile. “In a way, I look at it as respect, I think. Maybe not. Maybe I’m looking at it the wrong way. I never thought I’d be in a situation where the whole arena is booing you, but I didn’t mind.’’

He had a pair of assists in the win.

The Rangers will celebrate the 100th anniversary of the franchise’s first game Monday against Montreal. Their first opponent was the now-defunct Montreal Maroons.

Pablo Sandoval is officially hanging up his baseball jersey.

The three-time Giants World Series champ officially announced his retirement after 14 seasons in the majors, along with a stint in the Mexican League and two seasons with the Staten Island FerryHawks in the Atlantic League.

His last major league game took place in 2021 with the Braves.

Affectionately dubbed “Kung Fu Panda,” Sandoval played 11 seasons in MLB with the Giants, where he won the World Series in 2010, 2012 and 2014, and was named World Series MVP in 2012 after hitting three home runs in Game 1 against the Tigers.

Sandoval slashed .278/.330/.443 during his MLB career, which included time with the Giants, Red Sox and Braves, for whom he played 69 regular-season games during their 2021 World Series-winning campaign.

“Congratulations to Pablo Sandoval on a wonderful career!” MLB wrote in a post on X.

news.originalContent:
